bank.subject: evs
bank.topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
bank.prompt: Golu says: 'The kirana shop makes atta in the back of the shop. Farmers have nothing to do with it.' Fix Golu.

bank.answer: Farmers grow the wheat; it is harvested, threshed, cleaned and ground at a mill or chakki; the shop only sells the atta.

bank.subject: evs
bank.topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
bank.prompt: Why do farmers thresh and winnow wheat after harvesting it?
bank.prompt_hi: Fasal kaatne ke baad kisaan gehun ko thresh aur winnow (phatakna) kyon karte hain?
bank.answer: Threshing separates the grains from the stalks and ears; winnowing uses wind to blow away the light husk so only clean grain is left.

bank.subject: evs

bank.prompt: Sort these into plant-eaters and meat-eaters: cow, tiger, goat, eagle, rabbit, frog.

bank.answer: Plant-eaters: cow, goat, rabbit. Meat-eaters: tiger, eagle, frog (it eats insects).

bank.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
bank.prompt: Pine trees grow in cold, snowy mountains like those in Himachal. Their leaves are thin and needle-like. Why might needle leaves help in heavy snow?
bank.prompt_hi: Cheed (pine) ke ped Himachal jaise thande, barfeele pahadon mein ugte hain. Unke patte patle, sui jaise hote hain. Bhaari barf mein sui jaise patte kaise madad karte honge?
bank.answer: Snow slides off thin needles easily, so branches don't get loaded and break; needle leaves also lose less water in cold, dry winds.

bank.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
bank.prompt: Read this clue card: 'Very little rain, freezing winters, snowy mountains, people wear thick wool, eat barley and drink butter tea.' Which region is this? Point to it on the map and tell me which clues gave it away.
bank.prompt_hi: Ye clue card padho: 'Baarish bahut kam, kadaake ki sardi, barfeele pahaad, log mote oon ke kapde pehente hain, jau khaate hain aur butter wali chai peete hain.' Ye kaunsa ilaaka hai? Map pe dikhao aur batao kin clues se pata chala.
bank.answer: Ladakh, a cold desert in the far north of India; the clues are very little rain plus freezing cold, mountains and thick wool.

bank.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
bank.prompt: Here is Riya's sleep chart: Monday 10 hours, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 10, Thursday 6, Friday 10. Which days did she probably feel tired, and why?
bank.prompt_hi: Ye Riya ka sleep chart hai: Somvaar 10 ghante, Mangalvaar 7, Budhvaar 10, Guruvaar 6, Shukravaar 10. Kis din use shayad thakaan lagi hogi, aur kyon?
bank.answer: Tuesday and Thursday, because she slept much less than the 9 to 12 hours a child needs.

bank.subject: evs

bank.answer: Chewing the twig makes a soft brush that scrubs the teeth, and neem has bitter substances that people have long used to help keep the mouth clean and fight germs.

bank.subject: evs

bank.answer: Postman delivers letters and parcels; sweeper keeps the streets clean; vegetable seller brings fresh vegetables for people to buy.

bank.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
bank.prompt: A lotus grows in ponds. Its leaves are big, round and flat, with a waxy top where water drops roll off. How does this help the lotus?
bank.prompt_hi: Kamal talaab mein ugta hai. Uske patte bade, gol aur chapte hote hain, aur upar se mome jaise, jahan se paani ki boondein lud jaati hain. Isse kamal ko kya fayda hai?
bank.answer: The broad flat leaves rest on or above the water and catch lots of sunlight; the waxy coat keeps water from soaking or sitting on them.

bank.answer: Any three with sensible reasons, e.g. hospital (health), school (studies), market or kirana (food), bank or ATM (money), police station (safety).

bank.answer: A good answer names a real local place, describes a practice of care (not cutting the tree, cleaning festivals, rules about waste) and suggests a realistic action (not littering, joining a clean-up, using cloth bags, reminding visitors).

bank.answer: Trade and transport (goods, roads, railways, ports); sharing rivers and flood warnings; helping each other in disasters (such as the 2004 tsunami or the 2015 Nepal earthquake); tourism and pilgrimage; peace and security along borders.

bank.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain how the Mauryan empire rose and how it was governed, including Ashoka’s dhamma
bank.prompt: Why did Ashoka change his way of ruling after the Kalinga war?
bank.prompt_hi: Kalinga yuddh ke baad Ashoka ne raaj karne ka tareeka kyun badla?
bank.answer: He saw the huge suffering — deaths, injuries and people taken from their homes — and, as he wrote himself, felt deep regret; he gave up wars of conquest and chose to rule through dhamma.

bank.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe the emergence of janapadas and mahajanapadas and early cities
bank.prompt: Compare a mahajanapada ruled by a raja with a gana-sangha like the Vajjis: who decided, and how?
bank.prompt_hi: Raja wale mahajanapada aur Vajji jaise gana-sangha ki tulna karo: faisla kaun leta tha, aur kaise?
bank.answer: In a kingdom, one raja (often from one family) made the main decisions, collected taxes and led the army. In a gana-sangha, a group of leaders met in an assembly, discussed and decided together.

bank.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain why roads, railways, power and digital networks matter for development
bank.prompt: Compare road and rail infrastructure with digital infrastructure: what does each move, and give one example of each.
bank.prompt_hi: Sadak-rail infrastructure aur digital infrastructure ki tulna karo: har ek kya pahunchaata hai, aur har ek ka ek example do.
bank.answer: Roads and railways move people and goods (e.g. a highway carrying vegetables to a city). Digital infrastructure — mobile towers, optical fibre, the internet — moves information and money (e.g. online classes, UPI payments, telemedicine).

outcomes: Learner can compare monarchy, democracy, dictatorship and other forms of government
bank.prompt: Give three reasons why a country needs a government.
bank.prompt_hi: Teen kaaran batao ki ek desh ko sarkaar ki zaroorat kyun hoti hai.
bank.answer: To make rules and decisions for everyone, keep order and safety (including defence), settle disputes, and provide services like schools, roads, water and health care.

bank.topic: The State, the Government, and You
outcomes: Learner can distinguish the state and the government and describe how government affects daily life
bank.prompt: Where does the government get money for roads, schools and hospitals? Do children help pay?
bank.prompt_hi: Sarkaar ko sadakon, schoolon aur aspataalon ke liye paisa kahan se milta hai? Kya bachche bhi isme yogdaan dete hain?
bank.answer: Mainly from taxes: income tax paid by earners, taxes paid by businesses, and taxes such as GST included in the prices of many things we buy. So yes — when a family or child buys many goods, part of the price is tax that goes to the government.

bank.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe India’s major physical regions and how they shape ways of life

bank.answer: The unbroken western line is the Western Ghats (Sahyadri); the broken eastern line is the Eastern Ghats, cut through by big east-flowing rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, Mahanadi and Kaveri.

bank.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain the problems of barter and how money evolved, including digital payments

bank.answer: Key idea: barter needs a double coincidence of wants, has no common measure, cannot divide big items and goods spoil; money solves these by being a medium of exchange, a measure of value and a store of value, and it works because people trust it.

bank.answer: 1191: Prithviraj Chauhan defeated Muhammad Ghori (First Battle of Tarain). 1192: Ghori returned and defeated Prithviraj (Second Battle of Tarain), opening the way for rule from Delhi.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
served.prompt: What does a bank do?
served.prompt_hi: Bank kya-kya kaam karta hai?
served.answer: It keeps money safe, gives loans to people who need money, and pays savers a little extra called interest

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Places and services in a neighbourhood
outcomes: Learner can identify public places (post office, bank, hospital) and what they do
served.prompt: Where would you go to: post a rakhi to your cousin in another city? See a doctor for fever? Report a lost bicycle?
served.prompt_hi: Kahan jaoge: doosre shehar mein cousin ko rakhi bhejne? Bukhaar mein doctor ko dikhane? Khoyi hui cycle ki report karne?
served.answer: Post office; hospital, clinic or health centre; police station.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
served.prompt: Give two reasons why people save money.
served.prompt_hi: Log paise kyon bachaate hain? Do kaaran batao.
served.answer: Any two: to buy something bigger later, for emergencies such as illness, for the future such as studies, for festivals or trips.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
served.prompt: You put ₹500 in your bank account. What does the bank do with it?
served.prompt_hi: Tumne bank account mein ₹500 jama kiye. Bank un paison ka kya karta hai?
served.answer: Writes ₹500 in your account and uses savers' money to give loans; you can still take out ₹500 (plus interest) when you need it

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why people save money and where
served.prompt: Without looking back: name two places where we can save money, and one reason to save.
served.prompt_hi: Bina dekhe batao: paise bachaane ki do jagah, aur bachat ka ek kaaran.
served.answer: Places: a gullak (piggy bank), a bank savings account, a post office savings account. Reasons: the future, emergencies, buying something bigger.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
served.prompt: Draw (or describe) a bird that lives on water and eats fish. What beak and what feet will you give it?
served.prompt_hi: Ek aisi chidiya banao (ya batao) jo paani pe rehti hai aur machhli khaati hai. Usko kaisi chonch aur kaise pair doge?
served.answer: A beak suited to catching fish (long and pointed, or hooked at the tip) and webbed feet for swimming.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
served.prompt: A kingfisher has a long, sharp, pointed beak. What does it mostly eat?
served.prompt_hi: Kingfisher ki chonch lambi, nukeeli aur tez hoti hai. Woh zyadatar kya khaata hai?
served.answer: Fish, which it catches from the water

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can observe and record features like beaks, feet and leaf shapes and link them to how organisms live
served.prompt: A parrot has a strong, curved, hooked beak. What kind of food is it good for?
served.prompt_hi: Tote ki chonch mazboot, mudi hui aur hook jaisi hoti hai. Ye kis tarah ka khaana khaane ke liye achhi hai?
served.answer: Cracking nuts and hard seeds and biting into fruits.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
served.prompt: Sort these into plant-eaters and meat-eaters: cow, tiger, goat, eagle, rabbit, frog.
served.prompt_hi: Inhe ghaas-paat khaane wale aur maans khaane wale mein baanto: gaay, sher, bakri, cheel, khargosh, mendhak.
served.answer: Plant-eaters: cow, goat, rabbit. Meat-eaters: tiger, eagle, frog (it eats insects).

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
served.prompt: If all the earthworms in a garden disappeared, what would happen?
served.prompt_hi: Agar ek bageeche ke saare kenchue (earthworms) gayab ho jaayein, toh kya hoga?
served.answer: Dead leaves would break down slowly and the soil would get poorer, so plants would grow less well

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe simple food relationships in a garden or forest
served.prompt: Compare a cow's teeth and a tiger's teeth. How does each match what the animal eats?
served.prompt_hi: Gaay ke daant aur sher ke daant ki tulna karo. Dono ke daant unke khaane se kaise milte hain?
served.answer: A cow has broad flat teeth for grinding grass; a tiger has sharp pointed teeth for gripping and tearing meat.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
served.prompt: Name one community or movement in India known for protecting trees.
served.prompt_hi: India ki koi ek community ya andolan batao jo pedon ko bachaane ke liye jaana jaata hai.
served.answer: The Bishnoi community of Rajasthan, the Chipko movement of Uttarakhand, or villages that keep sacred groves.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
served.prompt: Many grandmothers keep dry neem leaves in stored grain. What does that do?
served.prompt_hi: Bahut si daadi-naani rakhe hue anaaj mein sookhe neem ke patte daalti hain. Isse kya hota hai?
served.answer: Neem leaves help keep insects away, so the grain stays safe; scientists have found insect-repelling substances in neem

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Traditional ways of living with nature
outcomes: Learner can give examples of local knowledge and practices that protect plants and animals
served.prompt: From last time: what did the people in the Chipko movement do, and why?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Chipko andolan mein logon ne kya kiya tha, aur kyon?
served.answer: They hugged trees to stop them from being cut down.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
served.prompt: Name one plant part we eat that is a root, one that is a stem, and one that is a leaf.
served.prompt_hi: Ek aisi cheez batao jo hum jad (root) ke roop mein khaate hain, ek tana (stem), aur ek patta.
served.answer: Root: carrot, radish or beetroot. Stem: sugarcane or potato (an underground stem). Leaf: spinach, methi or cabbage.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
served.prompt: Where did quinine, an old medicine for malaria, first come from?
served.prompt_hi: Quinine, jo malaria ki purani dawai hai, sabse pehle kahan se mili thi?
served.answer: From the bark of the cinchona tree

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can list uses of plants for food, medicine, shelter and craft
served.prompt: Look at your lunch thali: name each item and the plant or plant part it came from.
served.prompt_hi: Apni lunch ki thali dekho: har cheez ka naam batao aur woh kis paudhe ya paudhe ke kis hisse se aayi.
served.answer: e.g. roti: wheat seeds (grains); rice: rice seeds; dal: pulse seeds; aloo: potato, an underground stem; salt: not from a plant.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
served.prompt: Sort into energy-giving, body-building and protective: rice, dal, spinach, paneer, guava, roti.
served.prompt_hi: Inhe energy dene wale, body banane wale aur bachaane wale (protective) khaane mein baanto: chawal, dal, palak, paneer, amrood, roti.
served.answer: Energy-giving: rice, roti. Body-building: dal, paneer. Protective: spinach, guava.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
served.prompt: Which is the healthier lunch?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa lunch zyada healthy hai?
served.answer: Roti, dal, sabzi, curd and some salad

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can group foods by what they do for the body and plan a balanced meal
served.prompt: From last time: name two body-building foods a vegetarian child can eat.
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: do body-building khaane batao jo shakahari bachcha kha sakta hai.
served.answer: Any two of: dal, paneer, milk, curd, chana, soybean, rajma.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
served.prompt: Which of these are junk food: chips, roasted chana, cold drink, banana, instant noodles, sprouts chaat?
served.prompt_hi: Inmein se junk food kaunse hain: chips, bhune chane, cold drink, kela, instant noodles, sprouts chaat?
served.answer: Junk: chips, cold drink, instant noodles. Healthy: roasted chana, banana, sprouts chaat.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
served.prompt: Which is better for you: an orange or a packaged orange drink?
served.prompt_hi: Tumhare liye kya behtar hai: ek santra ya packet wali orange drink?
served.answer: The orange: it has fibre and no added sugar; the drink often has added sugar and little fibre

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can identify junk food and explain why it should be eaten rarely
served.prompt: Press a potato chip on a piece of plain paper for a minute, and do the same with a slice of raw cucumber. Predict: what will you see on the paper after you lift each one and wait a while?
served.prompt_hi: Saade kaagaz pe ek chips ko ek minute dabao, aur phir kheere ke ek tukde ko. Guess karo: dono hata ke thodi der baad kaagaz pe kya dikhega?
served.answer: The chip leaves an oily, see-through spot that does not dry away; the cucumber leaves a wet spot that dries. The chips have a lot of fat (oil).

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
served.prompt: About how many hours of sleep does a child of your age need each night?
served.prompt_hi: Tumhari umar ke bachche ko har raat lagbhag kitne ghante sona chahiye?
served.answer: About 9 to 12 hours.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
served.prompt: Your friend is sad because her pet fish died. What is true?
served.prompt_hi: Tumhari dost udaas hai kyonki uski pet machhli mar gayi. Kya sach hai?
served.answer: Feeling sad is normal; talking about it and being with people she trusts can help

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how sleep, exercise and talking about feelings help well-being
served.prompt: Two children have a test the next morning. One sleeps at 9:30 pm; the other watches a phone till midnight. Predict who will remember answers better and feel fresher.
served.prompt_hi: Do bachchon ka agle din test hai. Ek raat 9:30 baje so jaata hai, doosra aadhi raat tak phone dekhta hai. Guess karo, kise jawab zyada yaad rahenge aur kaun fresh mehsoos karega?
served.answer: The one who slept at 9:30: good sleep helps the brain store what was learnt and keeps you alert.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
served.prompt: Put these steps in order: grinding into atta, harvesting, sowing seeds, making roti, threshing.
served.prompt_hi: In steps ko sahi kram mein lagao: atta peesna, fasal kaatna, beej bona, roti banana, gehun ke daane alag karna (thresher).
served.answer: sowing seeds → harvesting → threshing → grinding into atta → making roti

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
served.prompt: There is leftover rice from dinner, kept covered in the fridge. What's a good choice?
served.prompt_hi: Raat ke khaane ka bacha hua chawal dhak ke fridge mein rakha hai. Achha kya rahega?
served.answer: Use it the next day, e.g. as lemon rice, since it was stored safely and smells fine

served.subject: evs
served.topic: Journey of food from farm to plate
outcomes: Learner can trace the steps grains go through to reach the plate and avoid wasting food
served.prompt: From last time: what happens at the chakki?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: chakki mein kya hota hai?
served.answer: Wheat grains are ground into flour (atta).

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
served.prompt: Which of these float in water and which sink: a steel spoon, a plastic bottle cap, a coin, a dry leaf, a stone, a piece of wood?
served.prompt_hi: Inmein se kya paani pe tairega aur kya doobega: steel ka chammach, plastic ki bottle ka dhakkan, sikka, sookha patta, patthar, lakdi ka tukda?
served.answer: Float: plastic bottle cap, dry leaf, wood. Sink: steel spoon, coin, stone.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
served.prompt: Which will sink: a big wooden log or a small steel coin?
served.prompt_hi: Kya doobega: lakdi ka bada lattha ya steel ka chhota sikka?
served.answer: The coin sinks and the log floats: the material matters, not just the weight

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can predict and test which objects float or sink and make a boat that floats
served.prompt: A big watermelon is much heavier than a small coin. Predict: which one will float in a big tub of water?
served.prompt_hi: Bada tarbooz chhote sikke se kahin zyada bhaari hai. Guess karo: paani ke bade tub mein kaun tairega?
served.answer: The watermelon floats; the coin sinks.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
served.prompt: What pushes or pulls each of these to make it move: a kite going up, a swing, a football?
served.prompt_hi: Inko kaun dhakelta ya kheenchta hai: upar jaati patang, jhoola, football?
served.answer: Kite: the wind pushes it up and the string pulls it. Swing: a push from someone or from your own legs. Football: a kick, which is a push.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
served.prompt: Why does a phirki at the mela spin?
served.prompt_hi: Mele ki phirki kyon ghoomti hai?
served.answer: Moving air pushes on its blades

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can make a paper spinner and explain what makes it turn faster or slower
served.prompt: From last time: what must happen for anything to start moving?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kisi bhi cheez ko chalna shuru karne ke liye kya hona zaroori hai?
served.answer: It must be pushed or pulled.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
served.prompt: Name two plant materials that paper can be made from.
served.prompt_hi: Do paudhon wali cheezein batao jinse kaagaz banta hai.
served.answer: Any two: wood, bamboo, sugarcane waste (bagasse), cotton rags, straw.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
served.prompt: How do we get paper?
served.prompt_hi: Kaagaz humein kaise milta hai?
served.answer: People break wood or other plant parts into fibres, make pulp with water, then spread, press and dry it

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can describe how paper is made from plants and recycle paper in class
served.prompt: Slowly tear a piece of newspaper and look closely at the torn edge (with a magnifying glass if you have one). Predict first: will the edge be smooth or hairy?
served.prompt_hi: Akhbaar ka ek tukda dheere se phaado aur phati hui kinaari ko dhyaan se dekho (magnifying glass ho toh usse). Pehle guess karo: kinaari chikni hogi ya roeydaar?
served.answer: Hairy or fuzzy: you can see tiny fibres from plants, which is what paper is made of.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
served.prompt: Sort into natural and human-made: wool, plastic bucket, stone, glass bottle, cotton, steel spoon.
served.prompt_hi: Inhe natural aur insaan ke banaye hue mein baanto: oon, plastic ki baalti, patthar, kaanch ki bottle, cotton, steel ka chammach.
served.answer: Natural: wool, stone, cotton. Human-made: plastic bucket, glass bottle, steel spoon.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
served.prompt: Plastic is made from crude oil, which comes from under the ground. So is plastic natural or human-made?
served.prompt_hi: Plastic crude oil se banta hai, jo zameen ke neeche se aata hai. Toh plastic natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua?
served.answer: Human-made: people change the oil completely in factories to make plastic

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can classify materials as natural or human-made
served.prompt: Is silk natural or human-made? What about nylon?
served.prompt_hi: Resham (silk) natural hai ya insaan ka banaya hua? Aur nylon?
served.answer: Silk is natural (from silkworm cocoons); nylon is human-made (made from oil in factories).

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
served.prompt: Match each place to its description. Places: Ladakh, the Thar desert, the Kerala coast, the Punjab plains. Descriptions: cold desert, hot desert, near the sea, flat land with rivers.
served.prompt_hi: Jagah ko uske varnan se milao. Jagah: Ladakh, Thar registaan, Kerala ka samandar kinara, Punjab ke maidaan. Varnan: thanda registaan, garam registaan, samandar ke paas, nadiyon wali samtal zameen.
served.answer: Ladakh: cold desert. Thar: hot desert. Kerala coast: near the sea. Punjab plains: flat land with rivers.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
served.prompt: Ladakh is very cold, with snowy mountains, and gets very little rain. Is it a desert?
served.prompt_hi: Ladakh bahut thanda hai, barfeele pahaad hain, aur baarish bahut kam hoti hai. Kya ye registaan (desert) hai?
served.answer: Yes: a desert is a place with very little rain, and Ladakh is a cold desert

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can compare food, houses and clothes of people in different regions of India and link them to climate
served.prompt: From last time: what is the one thing every desert has in common?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: har registaan mein kaunsi ek baat common hoti hai?
served.answer: Very little rain.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
served.prompt: Why are many houses in flood-prone parts of Assam built on bamboo stilts?
served.prompt_hi: Assam ke baadh wale ilaakon mein bahut se ghar baans ke khambhon (stilts) pe kyon bane hote hain?
served.answer: To stay above flood water and keep away from damp ground (and from crawling animals).

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
served.prompt: Why don't people in flood-prone parts of Assam just build ordinary houses on the ground?
served.prompt_hi: Assam ke baadh wale ilaakon mein log zameen pe aam ghar kyon nahi banaate?
served.answer: Houses on stilts keep homes above flood water and damp ground, so they suit Assam

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can explain why houses are built differently in different regions
served.prompt: Here is a description: 'A house on tall bamboo posts, with bamboo walls, a sloping thatch roof and a ladder to the door.' Draw it (or describe your drawing) and say what kind of place it suits.
served.prompt_hi: Ye varnan suno: 'Lambe baans ke khambhon pe ghar, baans ki deewarein, phoos ki dhalaan wali chhat, aur darwaze tak seedhi.' Iski drawing banao (ya batao kya banaoge) aur batao ye kis tarah ki jagah ke liye theek hai.
served.answer: A stilt house; it suits a place with heavy rain and floods, like parts of Assam.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
served.prompt: What do you need to make a shadow?
served.prompt_hi: Parchhai banane ke liye kya-kya chahiye?
served.answer: A light source, an object that blocks the light, and a surface for the shadow to fall on.

served.subject: evs
served.topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
served.prompt: In a completely dark room with no light at all, will your hand make a shadow?
served.prompt_hi: Bilkul andhere kamre mein, jahan zara bhi roshni nahi, kya tumhare haath ki parchhai banegi?
served.answer: No: a shadow needs light to be blocked; with no light there is no shadow

served.subject: evs
served.topic: The Sun and shadows during the day
outcomes: Learner can observe how shadows change in length and direction during the day
served.prompt: Hold a red ball in sunlight. Predict: what colour will its shadow be?
served.prompt_hi: Dhoop mein ek laal ball pakdo. Guess karo: uski parchhai kis rang ki hogi?
served.answer: Dark grey, not red: a shadow is just where the light is blocked.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
served.prompt: Diwali falls on Amavasya, a dark moonless night. About how many days later will the next Purnima come?
served.prompt_hi: Diwali Amavasya ki andheri raat ko hoti hai. Lagbhag kitne din baad agli Purnima aayegi?
served.answer: About 15 days later.

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
served.prompt: On a half-moon night, what is really happening?
served.prompt_hi: Aadhe chaand wali raat ko asal mein kya ho raha hota hai?
served.answer: The Moon is still round; we are seeing only half of its sunlit side

served.subject: evs
outcomes: Learner can record the Moon’s shape over a month and describe the pattern
served.prompt: What do we call the night when we see the full round Moon, and the night when we can't see the Moon at all?
served.prompt_hi: Jis raat poora gol chaand dikhta hai use kya kehte hain, aur jis raat chaand bilkul nahi dikhta use kya?
served.answer: Full Moon: Purnima. No Moon visible: Amavasya (new moon).

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can recite the poem with rhythm and expression and say what it describes (theme: teamwork)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Listen: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Which word fits: 'true' or 'tight'?
served.prompt_hi: Suno: 'One small stick will snap in two, / Tie ten together, strong and ___!' Kaunsa word fit hoga, 'true' ya 'tight'? Rhyme ka dhyaan rakho.
served.answer: true

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can recite the poem with rhythm and expression and say what it describes (theme: teamwork)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Say them aloud: 'two' and 'true'. Do they rhyme?
served.prompt_hi: Zor se bolo: 'two' aur 'true'. Spelling mat dekho, sirf suno. Kya ye rhyme karte hain?
served.answer: Yes, they end with the same sound

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can recite the poem with rhythm and expression and say what it describes (theme: teamwork)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: 'two' and 'true' are spelt differently at the end. Say them aloud. Do they rhyme?
served.prompt_hi: 'two' aur 'true' ki spelling alag hai. Dono ko zor se bolo. Kya rhyme karte hain?
served.answer: yes

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the story aloud, retell the events in order and share what they liked (theme: a village boy and his friends)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Put these in order: (a) They found Gauri in the bushes. (b) Gauri did not come home. (c) Meena heard a tinkle. Which comes first?
served.prompt_hi: In teeno ko order mein lagao: (a) They found Gauri in the bushes. (b) Gauri did not come home. (c) Meena heard a tinkle. Pehle kya hua?
served.answer: b

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the story aloud, retell the events in order and share what they liked (theme: a village boy and his friends)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Yesterday Gopu ___ to the river. Is it 'goed' or 'went'?
served.prompt_hi: Kal Gopu river pe ___. 'goed' bolenge ya 'went'?
served.answer: went

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the story aloud, retell the events in order and share what they liked (theme: a village boy and his friends)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Where did the friends find Gauri?
served.prompt_hi: Doston ko Gauri kahan mili?
served.answer: In thorny bushes in the mango grove

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the text and answer questions about its main ideas (theme: road safety)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: What does a red traffic light mean?
served.prompt_hi: Laal batti ka matlab kya hota hai?
served.answer: Stop

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the text and answer questions about its main ideas (theme: road safety)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own
served.prompt: Which is the right way to say it: 'Don't run on the road.' or 'Not run on the road.'?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi tareeka hai: 'Don't run on the road.' ya 'Not run on the road.'? Hindi mein 'mat bhaago' hota hai, English mein?
served.answer: Don't run on the road.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the text and answer questions about its main ideas (theme: road safety)
Learner can use new words from the lesson in sentences of their own

served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sawaal test kiya ja sakta hai: (A) 'Kya aam sabse tasty fruit hai?' ya (B) 'Kya aam newspaper mein lapetne se jaldi pakte hain ya khule mein rakhne se?' Doosra wala alag kyon hai?
served.answer: B is testable: we can wrap some mangoes, leave others open and watch which ripen first. A is an opinion; people can disagree and no test can settle it.

served.answer: Type of cloth | Time taken to dry (minutes); a notes column is optional.

served.answer: Table: Cloth | Time to dry (min): Cotton 30, Nylon 20, Wool 50. Nylon dried fastest.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify plants by stem, height and branching
served.prompt: Gently press the stem of a mint (pudina) plant, then touch the trunk of a mango or neem tree. How are the two stems different?

served.answer: The mint stem is soft, thin and green and bends easily; the tree trunk is hard, thick, woody and brown.

served.answer: The coriander stem bends easily because it is a soft green herb stem; the hibiscus branch is hard and woody.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can measure curved lengths with a thread
served.prompt: How can you find the length of a curved line on paper?
served.prompt_hi: Kaagaz pe bani tedhi-medhi line ki lambai kaise pata karoge?
served.answer: Lay a thread along it, straighten it, measure the thread

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can measure curved lengths with a thread
served.prompt: A curved line's two ends are 8 cm apart in a straight line. Predict: will a thread laid along the curve measure less than, equal to, or more than 8 cm?
served.prompt_hi: Ek tedhi line ke dono sire seedhe 8 cm door hain. Guess karo: line ke saath bichhaya dhaaga 8 cm se kam, barabar ya zyada naapega?
served.answer: More than 8 cm; a curve between two points is longer than the straight line joining them.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe motion as linear, circular or oscillatory using a reference point
served.prompt: What is a reference point? Give an example.
served.prompt_hi: Reference point kya hota hai? Ek example do.
served.answer: A fixed object or place we compare positions with to decide if something is moving, e.g. a tree beside the road, the platform or a signboard.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe motion as linear, circular or oscillatory using a reference point
served.prompt: You are sitting in a moving train. Are you moving?
served.prompt_hi: Tum chalti train mein baithe ho. Kya tum chal rahe ho?
served.answer: It depends: at rest to my seat, moving to the platform

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe motion as linear, circular or oscillatory using a reference point
served.prompt: Predict: Riya sits in a moving bus and her friend Aman stands at the bus stop. Will Aman say Riya is moving? Will the boy sitting next to Riya say she is moving?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: Riya chalti bus mein baithi hai aur Aman bus stop pe khada hai. Kya Aman kahega Riya chal rahi hai? Riya ke bagal wala ladka kya kahega?
served.answer: Aman says she is moving, because her position changes compared with the bus stop; the boy next to her says she is at rest, because her position doesn't change compared with him.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test properties like hardness, lustre, solubility, transparency and float-sink
served.prompt: Sort into transparent, translucent and opaque: clear glass, butter paper, a wooden board, clean water, a steel plate, frosted bathroom glass.
served.prompt_hi: Transparent, translucent aur opaque mein baanto: saaf kaanch, butter paper, lakdi ka phatta, saaf paani, steel ki plate, bathroom ka dhundhla kaanch.
served.answer: Transparent: clear glass, clean water. Translucent: butter paper, frosted glass. Opaque: wooden board, steel plate.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test properties like hardness, lustre, solubility, transparency and float-sink
served.prompt: Sugar and fine white sand look alike. You stir each into a glass of water. What happens?
served.prompt_hi: Cheeni aur safed baareek ret dikhne mein ek jaise hain. Dono ko alag-alag glass paani mein ghola. Kya hoga?
served.answer: Sugar dissolves; the sand settles at the bottom

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test properties like hardness, lustre, solubility, transparency and float-sink
served.prompt: What is lustre? Name two materials that have it.
served.prompt_hi: Lustre kya hai? Do materials batao jinme ye hota hai.
served.answer: Lustre is the shine on a surface; metals such as copper, steel, gold, silver and aluminium have it, especially when freshly polished or cut.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can group materials by properties and relate properties to uses
served.prompt: Name the material each object is made of: a notebook, a lota, a raincoat, a window pane.
served.prompt_hi: Har object kis material se bana hai, batao: notebook, lota, raincoat, khidki ka sheesha.
served.answer: Notebook: paper. Lota: brass, copper or steel. Raincoat: plastic or another waterproof material. Window pane: glass.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can group materials by properties and relate properties to uses
served.prompt: Which of these is a material, not an object?
served.prompt_hi: Inme se kaunsa material hai, object nahi?
served.answer: Wood

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can group materials by properties and relate properties to uses
served.prompt: A steel spoon and a wooden spoon are the same object made of different materials. Name one property where they differ and one job each is better for.
served.prompt_hi: Steel ki chammach aur lakdi ki chammach, object ek hi hai par material alag. Ek property batao jisme farak hai, aur ek kaam jiske liye har ek behtar hai.
served.answer: For example: heat passes through steel easily (it gets hot in hot dal) but not through wood; wood is better for stirring hot food in a pan, steel is better for eating and easy to clean. Steel is shiny and wood is dull.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain why touch is not reliable for hotness and use temperature in °C
served.prompt: Why can't we always trust our hand to tell how hot something is?
served.prompt_hi: Hum hamesha apne haath pe bharosa kyon nahi kar sakte ki koi cheez kitni garam hai?
served.answer: What we feel depends on how warm or cold our hand already is; touch gives no number, and it is unsafe for very hot things.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain why touch is not reliable for hotness and use temperature in °C
served.prompt: A steel spoon and a wooden spoon have been lying on the same table all day. A thermometer touches each. What will it show?
served.prompt_hi: Steel aur lakdi ki chammach poore din ek hi mez pe padi hain. Thermometer dono ko chhoota hai. Kya dikhayega?
served.answer: Both are at the same (room) temperature

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain why touch is not reliable for hotness and use temperature in °C
served.prompt: Predict: keep your left hand in cold water and your right hand in comfortably warm water (never hot!) for a minute, then put both hands into the same lukewarm water. How will it feel to each hand?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: left haath thande paani mein aur right haath halke garam paani mein (garam bilkul nahi!) ek minute rakho, phir dono ek hi gungune paani mein daalo. Har haath ko kaisa lagega?
served.answer: The left (cold) hand will feel the lukewarm water as warm; the right (warm) hand will feel it as cool, even though it is the same water.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can read clinical and laboratory thermometers safely and correctly
served.prompt: What is the range of a clinical thermometer, and why doesn't it need a bigger range?
served.prompt_hi: Clinical thermometer ki range kya hai, aur ise isse badi range ki zaroorat kyon nahi?
served.answer: About 35 °C to 42 °C; human body temperature stays within this range.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can read clinical and laboratory thermometers safely and correctly
served.prompt: Why should you NOT put a clinical thermometer in boiling water?
served.prompt_hi: Clinical thermometer ko ubalte paani mein kyon NAHI daalna chahiye?
served.answer: Its scale stops near 42 °C, so it can't show 100 °C

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can read clinical and laboratory thermometers safely and correctly
served.prompt: From last time: what is normal human body temperature in °C?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: insaan ke shareer ka saamaanya temperature °C mein kitna hota hai?
served.answer: About 37 °C.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
served.topic: Solid, liquid and gas states of water
outcomes: Learner can describe the three states of water and changes between them
served.prompt: Name the three states of water and give one example of each from your home.
served.prompt_hi: Paani ki teen avasthaayein batao aur har ek ka ghar se ek example do.
served.answer: Solid: ice (ice cubes in the freezer). Liquid: water (from the tap, in a lota). Gas: water vapour (invisible; it rises from wet clothes drying and from boiling water).

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
served.topic: Solid, liquid and gas states of water
outcomes: Learner can describe the three states of water and changes between them
served.prompt: What is inside the big bubbles that rise when water is boiling hard?
served.prompt_hi: Jab paani zor se ubalta hai, toh upar uthne wale bade bulbulon mein kya hota hai?
served.answer: Water vapour (water as gas)

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
served.topic: Solid, liquid and gas states of water
outcomes: Learner can describe the three states of water and changes between them
served.prompt: Predict: you pour a glass of water into a flat plate, then from the plate into a tall bottle. Does the amount of water change? Does its shape change?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek glass paani ko pehle chapti plate mein daalo, phir plate se lambi botal mein. Kya paani ki matra badlegi? Kya uska aakaar badlega?
served.answer: The shape changes to fit each container, but the amount (volume) of water stays the same.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can explain evaporation and condensation using everyday examples
served.prompt: What is evaporation? Give two examples from home.
served.prompt_hi: Evaporation (vaashpikaran) kya hai? Ghar se do example do.
served.answer: Liquid water changing into water vapour. Examples: clothes drying, a wet floor drying, water in a plate drying up, wet hair drying, puddles drying.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can explain evaporation and condensation using everyday examples
served.prompt: You put ice and a few drops of food colour into a steel tumbler. Drops form on the outside. What colour are they?
served.prompt_hi: Steel ke tumbler mein barf aur khaane ke rang ki kuch boondein daali. Bahar boondein ban gayin. Unka rang kya hoga?
served.answer: Clear, because they come from water vapour in the air

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can explain evaporation and condensation using everyday examples
served.prompt: Predict: a spoonful of water in a steel plate is left on the table, not in the sun and not heated. After a day, what happens?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: steel ki plate mein ek chammach paani mez pe rakha hai, na dhoop mein, na garam kiya. Ek din baad kya hoga?
served.answer: It evaporates and the plate becomes dry, even though the water never boiled.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can test how temperature, wind and surface area affect evaporation and explain cooling by evaporation
served.prompt: Name four things that make water evaporate faster.
served.prompt_hi: Chaar cheezein batao jo paani ko jaldi evaporate karti hain.
served.answer: Higher temperature (heat or sun), wind (moving air), a larger surface area (spreading the water out) and dry air (low humidity).

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can test how temperature, wind and surface area affect evaporation and explain cooling by evaporation
served.prompt: Two clay pots: one plain, one completely coated with paint so water can't seep out. Which cools water better?
served.prompt_hi: Do mitti ke ghade: ek saada, ek poora paint se dhaka hua taaki paani bahar na rise. Kaun paani ko behtar thanda karega?
served.answer: The plain one; water seeps out and evaporates

served.subject: science
served.chapter: A Journey through States of Water
outcomes: Learner can test how temperature, wind and surface area affect evaporation and explain cooling by evaporation
served.prompt: Predict: equal amounts of water are put in a wide plate and in a narrow glass, side by side on the same table. Which dries first?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: utna hi paani ek chaudi plate mein aur ek patle glass mein, ek hi mez pe saath rakha. Kaun pehle sookhega?
served.answer: The wide plate, because the water has a larger surface open to the air.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can choose a suitable method to separate mixtures based on differences in size, weight and other properties
served.prompt: Give two reasons why we separate mixtures.
served.prompt_hi: Mishran ko alag karne ke do kaaran batao.
served.answer: To remove harmful or unwanted things (stones, husk, dirt) and to get the useful parts (grain, butter, salt).

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can choose a suitable method to separate mixtures based on differences in size, weight and other properties
served.prompt: A farmer has a mixture of grain, husk and a few small stones. What should he do?
served.prompt_hi: Ek kisaan ke paas anaaj, bhoosa aur kuch chhote pattharon ka mishran hai. Use kya karna chahiye?
served.answer: Winnow out husk, then handpick or sieve stones

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can choose a suitable method to separate mixtures based on differences in size, weight and other properties
served.prompt: Which method would you use to remove small stones from a plate of dal?
served.prompt_hi: Dal ki thali se chhote kankar nikaalne ke liye kaunsa tareeka use karoge?
served.answer: Handpicking.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can separate insoluble solids from liquids and dissolved solids by evaporation
served.prompt: What is decantation?
served.prompt_hi: Decantation (niraharan) kya hai?
served.answer: Gently pouring off the clearer liquid on top without disturbing the solid that has settled at the bottom.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can separate insoluble solids from liquids and dissolved solids by evaporation
served.prompt: Salt is stirred into water until you can't see it. You leave the water in a plate in the sun for two days. What will you find?
served.prompt_hi: Paani mein namak itna ghola ki dikhna band ho gaya. Ye paani plate mein do din dhoop mein rakho. Kya milega?
served.answer: White salt crystals left after the water evaporates

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life
outcomes: Learner can separate insoluble solids from liquids and dissolved solids by evaporation
served.prompt: Predict: you stir muddy water in a glass and leave it undisturbed for an hour. What will you see?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: glass mein matmaila paani hila ke ek ghante tak bina chhede rakho. Kya dikhega?
served.answer: The mud and sand settle at the bottom (sedimentation), with clearer water on top, though it may still be a little cloudy.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can list features that distinguish living from non-living things (growth, respiration, response, reproduction)
served.prompt: List five features that all living things show.
served.prompt_hi: Paanch khoobiyan batao jo saare jeevit cheezon mein hoti hain.
served.answer: Any five: need food, grow, respire, respond to changes around them, get rid of wastes, reproduce, have a life span and die.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can list features that distinguish living from non-living things (growth, respiration, response, reproduction)
served.prompt: A car moves and uses petrol. Is it living?
served.prompt_hi: Car chalti hai aur petrol use karti hai. Kya woh jeevit hai?
served.answer: No; it can't grow, reproduce or respond on its own

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can list features that distinguish living from non-living things (growth, respiration, response, reproduction)
served.prompt: Make a table with the features grows, needs food, respires, responds and reproduces as rows, and a cow, a mango tree and a car as columns. Fill in ✓ or ✗.
served.prompt_hi: Ek table banao: rows mein 'badhta hai, khaana chahiye, shwasan karta hai, pratikriya deta hai, prajanan karta hai', aur columns mein gaay, aam ka ped aur car. ✓ ya ✗ bharo.
served.answer: Cow: ✓ for all five. Mango tree: ✓ for all five. Car: ✗ for all five (fuel is not food, and it doesn't grow, respire, respond on its own or reproduce).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can design a fair test for the conditions needed for seeds to germinate
served.prompt: What three conditions do seeds need to germinate?
served.prompt_hi: Beejon ko ankurit hone ke liye kaunsi teen cheezein chahiye?
served.answer: Water, air and suitable warmth.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can design a fair test for the conditions needed for seeds to germinate
served.prompt: Moong seeds wrapped in a wet cloth are kept inside a dark kitchen box. Will they sprout?
served.prompt_hi: Geele kapde mein lipte moong ke daane rasoi ke andhere dabbe mein rakhe hain. Kya woh ankurit honge?
served.answer: Yes; they need water, air and warmth, not soil

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can design a fair test for the conditions needed for seeds to germinate
served.prompt: From last time: does a seed need soil to germinate?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kya beej ko ankurit hone ke liye mitti chahiye?
served.answer: No; it needs water, air and warmth.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Life cycles of plants and animals
outcomes: Learner can describe the life cycles of a plant, a mosquito and a frog
served.prompt: Put a mango plant's life cycle in order: flowers, seed, fruit, seedling, adult tree.
served.prompt_hi: Aam ke paudhe ka jeevan-chakra kram mein lagao: phool, beej, phal, chhota paudha, bada ped.
served.answer: Seed → seedling → adult tree → flowers → fruit (with a seed inside) → seed again.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Life cycles of plants and animals
outcomes: Learner can describe the life cycles of a plant, a mosquito and a frog
served.prompt: What will the tadpoles in a pond become?
served.prompt_hi: Talaab ke tadpole aage chalke kya banenge?
served.answer: Frogs

served.subject: science
served.topic: Life cycles of plants and animals
outcomes: Learner can describe the life cycles of a plant, a mosquito and a frog
served.prompt: A farmer saves seeds from this year's best tomatoes to plant next year. Use the plant life cycle to explain why this works.
served.prompt_hi: Ek kisaan iss saal ke sabse achhe tamatar ke beej agle saal ke liye bacha ke rakhta hai. Paudhe ke jeevan-chakra se samjhao ye kyon kaam karta hai.
served.answer: The fruits contain seeds; next season the seeds germinate into seedlings, grow into plants, flower and make fruits again, so the cycle repeats.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Air, water, sunlight, soil and forests
outcomes: Learner can identify natural resources and their uses
served.prompt: What is a natural resource? Name five.
served.prompt_hi: Prakritik sansaadhan kya hai? Paanch naam batao.
served.answer: Something from nature that living things use. Examples: air, water, sunlight, soil, forests (also minerals, coal, petroleum).

served.subject: science
served.topic: Air, water, sunlight, soil and forests
outcomes: Learner can identify natural resources and their uses
served.prompt: Is air a natural resource?
served.prompt_hi: Kya hawa ek prakritik sansaadhan hai?
served.answer: Yes; all living things need it, and wind is useful

served.subject: science
served.topic: Air, water, sunlight, soil and forests
outcomes: Learner can identify natural resources and their uses
served.prompt: Compare air and a bottle of packaged drinking water. You pay for one but not the other. Are both resources? Why?
served.prompt_hi: Hawa aur packed peene ke paani ki botal compare karo. Ek ke paise dete ho, doosre ke nahi. Kya dono sansaadhan hain? Kyon?
served.answer: Yes, both: a resource is anything useful from nature, whether we pay for it or not, and we can't live without air even for minutes.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify resources as renewable or non-renewable and suggest ways to use them wisely
served.prompt: Sort into renewable and non-renewable: sunlight, coal, wind, petroleum, water, natural gas.
served.prompt_hi: Renewable aur non-renewable mein baanto: dhoop, koyla, hawa, petroleum, paani, prakritik gas.
served.answer: Renewable: sunlight, wind, water. Non-renewable: coal, petroleum, natural gas.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify resources as renewable or non-renewable and suggest ways to use them wisely
served.prompt: In some Indian cities, borewells have dried up even though it rains every year. Why?
served.prompt_hi: Bharat ke kuch shehron mein har saal baarish hone ke baad bhi borewell sookh gaye. Kyon?
served.answer: More groundwater was pumped than rain refilled

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify resources as renewable or non-renewable and suggest ways to use them wisely
served.prompt: From last time: name one renewable and one non-renewable source of energy.
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: urja ka ek renewable aur ek non-renewable source batao.
served.answer: Renewable: sunlight, wind or flowing water. Non-renewable: coal, petroleum or natural gas.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can identify bright stars and constellations and explain why stars appear to move
served.prompt: What is a star? Name the star nearest to Earth.
served.prompt_hi: Taara kya hota hai? Dharti ke sabse paas wala taara kaunsa hai?
served.answer: A huge ball of very hot, glowing gas that gives out its own light. The Sun is the nearest star.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can identify bright stars and constellations and explain why stars appear to move
served.prompt: Why do stars look like tiny dots?
served.prompt_hi: Taare chhote-chhote bindu jaise kyon dikhte hain?
served.answer: Because they are huge but extremely far away

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can identify bright stars and constellations and explain why stars appear to move
served.prompt: Predict: how does a big street lamp look from 5 km away at night, compared with from 50 metres? What does this tell you about stars?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: raat mein ek badi street light 5 km door se kaisi dikhegi, 50 metre ke mukaable? Isse taaron ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai?
served.answer: From far away it looks like a tiny point of light; stars look tiny because they are very far away, even though they are huge.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can name planets in order and compare their sizes and distances
served.prompt: Name the eight planets in order, starting from the one nearest the Sun.
served.prompt_hi: Suraj ke sabse paas wale se shuru karke aathon grahon ke naam kram se batao.
served.answer: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can name planets in order and compare their sizes and distances
served.prompt: Why does the Moon shine at night?
served.prompt_hi: Chaand raat mein kyon chamakta hai?
served.answer: It reflects sunlight that falls on it

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can name planets in order and compare their sizes and distances
served.prompt: Make up your own sentence where each word starts with the first letter of a planet, in order: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.
served.prompt_hi: Apna ek vaakya banao jiska har shabd grahon ke pehle akshar se, kram se, shuru ho: M, V, E, M, J, S, U, N.
served.answer: Any sentence whose word initials are M V E M J S U N in order, e.g. 'My Very Educated Mother Just Served Us Noodles'.

served.subject: science
served.topic: The Milky Way and the universe
outcomes: Learner can describe the Milky Way as a galaxy and our place in the universe
served.prompt: What is a galaxy? What is the name of our galaxy?
served.prompt_hi: Galaxy (aakashganga) kya hoti hai? Hamari galaxy ka naam kya hai?
served.answer: A huge collection of billions of stars with gas and dust. Ours is the Milky Way (Akashganga).

served.subject: science
served.topic: The Milky Way and the universe
outcomes: Learner can describe the Milky Way as a galaxy and our place in the universe
served.prompt: Why does the Sun look bigger and brighter than all the other stars?
served.prompt_hi: Suraj baaki saare taaron se bada aur chamakdaar kyon dikhta hai?
served.answer: It is the nearest star; many are far bigger

served.subject: science
served.topic: The Milky Way and the universe
outcomes: Learner can describe the Milky Way as a galaxy and our place in the universe
served.prompt: From last time: is a light-year a measure of time or of distance?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: light-year samay ka naap hai ya doori ka?
served.answer: Distance: how far light travels in one year.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: hard work over shortcuts)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: In 'A Bottle of Dew', what did the sage ask Rama Natha to collect, and how much of it?
served.prompt_hi: 'A Bottle of Dew' mein sage ne Rama Natha ko kya collect karne ko kaha, aur kitna?
served.answer: Dew from the leaves of banana plants, five litres of it

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: hard work over shortcuts)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: In 'A Bottle of Dew', where did the gold coins in Madhumati's box come from?
served.prompt_hi: 'A Bottle of Dew' mein Madhumati ke box ke gold coins asal mein kahaan se aaye? Dhyaan se socho.
served.answer: From selling the bananas they grew over six years

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: hard work over shortcuts)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Put these in order: (a) Nothing happened to the copper vessel. (b) The sage asked for five litres of dew. (c) Madhumati opened a box of gold coins. (d) Rama Natha planted rows of banana plants.
served.prompt_hi: In events ko sahi order mein lagao: (a) Nothing happened to the copper vessel. (b) The sage asked for five litres of dew. (c) Madhumati opened a box of gold coins. (d) Rama Natha planted rows of banana plants.
served.answer: b, d, a, c

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: flattery)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: In the poem 'The Raven and the Fox', which word rhymes with 'beak': seek, break or back?
served.prompt_hi: Poem 'The Raven and the Fox' mein 'beak' ke saath kaunsa word rhyme karta hai: seek, break ya back? Bolke dekho.
served.answer: seek

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: flattery)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Your coach says, 'Your bowling has improved because you practised.' Is this flattery?
served.prompt_hi: Tumhara coach kehta hai, 'Your bowling has improved because you practised.' Kya ye flattery hai?
served.answer: No: it is honest, and he wants nothing from you

served.subject: english

served.prompt_hi: Riya kehti hai, 'Meri dadi kehti hain neem ke patte rakhe anaaj se keede door rakhte hain, toh ye sach hi hoga.' Arjun kehta hai, 'Do dibbe mein anaaj rakhte hain, ek mein neem ke patte, ek mein nahi, aur ek mahine baad dono dekhte hain.' Kiska tareeka scientific evidence deta hai, aur kyon?
