served.chapter: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral
outcomes: Learner can explain neutralisation and its everyday uses
served.prompt: What do we call the reaction in which an acid and a base cancel each other's effect?
served.prompt_hi: Jab acid aur base ek doosre ka asar khatam kar dete hain, us reaction ko kya kehte hain?
served.answer: Neutralisation.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral
outcomes: Learner can explain neutralisation and its everyday uses
served.prompt: When hydrochloric acid is neutralised by exactly the right amount of sodium hydroxide, what forms?
served.prompt_hi: Jab hydrochloric acid ko bilkul sahi maatra mein sodium hydroxide se neutralise karte hain, toh kya banta hai?
served.answer: Common salt and water

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral
outcomes: Learner can explain neutralisation and its everyday uses
served.prompt: What two things are formed when an acid neutralises a base? What else is given out?
served.prompt_hi: Jab acid aur base ka neutralisation hota hai toh kaunsi do cheezein banti hain? Aur kya nikalta hai?
served.answer: A salt and water are formed, and heat is given out.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can build a simple circuit and explain why the bulb glows only when the circuit is closed
served.prompt: An electric cell has a small metal cap at one end and a flat metal disc at the other. Which is the positive terminal and which is the negative?
served.prompt_hi: Ek electric cell ke ek sire pe chhota metal cap hai aur doosre pe chapti metal disc. Kaunsa positive terminal hai aur kaunsa negative?
served.answer: The metal cap is the positive (+) terminal; the flat metal disc is the negative (−) terminal.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can build a simple circuit and explain why the bulb glows only when the circuit is closed
served.prompt: A wire goes from the + terminal of a cell to the bottom tip of a bulb. Nothing is joined to the − terminal. Will the bulb glow?
served.prompt_hi: Ek taar cell ke + terminal se bulb ke neeche wale tip tak jaata hai. − terminal se kuch nahi juda. Kya bulb jalega?
served.answer: No, there must be a complete loop back to the other terminal of the cell

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can build a simple circuit and explain why the bulb glows only when the circuit is closed
served.prompt: Riddhi's worksheet says: 'The bulb glows because electricity comes from the bulb and goes into the cell.' Spot the mistake.
served.prompt_hi: Riddhi ki worksheet mein likha hai: 'Bulb isliye jalta hai kyonki bijli bulb se nikal ke cell mein jaati hai.' Galti pakdo.
served.answer: The cell is the source: it pushes current around the circuit through the bulb. The bulb does not make electricity; it changes electrical energy into light and heat.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can draw circuit diagrams using standard symbols and use a switch
served.prompt: Describe the circuit symbol for an electric cell. Which side is positive?
served.prompt_hi: Electric cell ka circuit symbol kaisa hota hai? Kaunsi side positive hai?
served.answer: Two parallel lines: a longer thin line and a shorter thick line; the longer line is the positive terminal.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can draw circuit diagrams using standard symbols and use a switch
served.prompt: In a circuit with a cell, a bulb and a switch, what does pressing the switch to ON do?
served.prompt_hi: Cell, bulb aur switch wale circuit mein switch ON karne se kya hota hai?
served.answer: It closes the gap so current from the cell can flow around the loop

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can draw circuit diagrams using standard symbols and use a switch
served.prompt: How is an open switch drawn differently from a closed switch in a circuit diagram?
served.prompt_hi: Circuit diagram mein khula (open) switch band (closed) switch se alag kaise banaya jaata hai?
served.answer: An open switch is drawn with a gap in the line (the lever not touching across); a closed switch is drawn with the gap bridged so the line is continuous.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test materials and classify them as conductors or insulators
served.prompt: How does a tester made of a cell, a bulb and two wires with a gap tell you whether a material is a conductor?
served.prompt_hi: Cell, bulb aur gap wale do taar se bana tester kaise batata hai ki koi material conductor hai?
served.answer: Touch the two free wire ends to the material: if the bulb glows, current passes through the material and closes the circuit, so it is a conductor; if not, it is an insulator.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test materials and classify them as conductors or insulators
served.prompt: Why must you never touch a switch with wet hands?
served.prompt_hi: Geele haathon se switch kabhi kyon nahi chhoona chahiye?
served.answer: Water on the skin can let current pass through your body, giving a dangerous shock

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can test materials and classify them as conductors or insulators
served.prompt: Predict, then check with your cell-and-bulb tester: will a steel hairpin make the bulb glow? A plastic button? A one-rupee coin?
served.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo, phir apne cell-bulb tester se check karo: kya steel ka hairpin bulb jalaayega? Plastic ka button? Ek rupaye ka sikka?
served.answer: The hairpin and the coin make it glow because they are metals; the plastic button does not, because plastic is an insulator.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can compare metals and non-metals for malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction
served.prompt: Which property of metals lets aluminium be made into thin foil for wrapping rotis?
served.prompt_hi: Metals ki kaunsi property ki wajah se aluminium ko roti lapetne wali patli foil mein banaya ja sakta hai?
served.answer: Malleability: metals can be beaten or pressed into thin sheets.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can compare metals and non-metals for malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction
served.prompt: Which statement is true?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsi baat sahi hai?
served.answer: Mercury, once used in thermometers, is a metal that is liquid at room temperature

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can compare metals and non-metals for malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction
served.prompt: Which property lets copper be drawn into thin wires, and which property makes a temple bell ring?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsi property ki wajah se copper ko patle taar mein kheencha ja sakta hai, aur kaunsi property mandir ki ghanti ko bajaati hai?
served.answer: Ductility lets copper be drawn into wires; sonority makes a metal bell ring.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
served.topic: Effect of air and water on metals
outcomes: Learner can describe rusting of iron and how it can be prevented
served.prompt: Which two things from the surroundings does iron need in order to rust?
served.prompt_hi: Lohe ko jung lagne ke liye aas-paas ki kaunsi do cheezon ki zaroorat hoti hai?
served.answer: Oxygen (from the air) and water (moisture).

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
served.topic: Effect of air and water on metals
outcomes: Learner can describe rusting of iron and how it can be prevented
served.prompt: Can you wash the rust off an old iron gate with soap and water and get all the original iron back?
served.prompt_hi: Kya purane lohe ke gate ka jung sabun-paani se dho ke saara original loha waapas mil sakta hai?
served.answer: No, rust is a new substance made from the iron itself; the iron underneath has become thinner

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
served.topic: Effect of air and water on metals
outcomes: Learner can describe rusting of iron and how it can be prevented
served.prompt: Predict: if an iron nail rusts completely and you collect every bit of the rust, will the rust weigh more than, less than or the same as the original nail?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar ek lohe ki keel poori tarah jung kha jaaye aur tum saara jung ikattha kar lo, toh jung ka wazan original keel se zyada hoga, kam hoga ya barabar?
served.answer: More, because oxygen and water from the air have combined with the iron to make the rust.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can explain why non-metals like oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential
served.prompt: Name two non-metals that are gases and one that is a solid.
served.prompt_hi: Do aise non-metals batao jo gas hain aur ek jo solid hai.
served.answer: Gases: for example oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, chlorine or helium. Solid: for example carbon, sulphur, iodine or phosphorus.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can explain why non-metals like oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential
served.prompt: Which statement about non-metals is true?
served.prompt_hi: Non-metals ke baare mein kaunsi baat sahi hai?
served.answer: Our bodies, the air we breathe and our food are built mostly from non-metals like oxygen, carbon, hydrogen and nitrogen

served.subject: science
served.chapter: The World of Metals and Non-metals
outcomes: Learner can explain why non-metals like oxygen, carbon and nitrogen are essential
served.prompt: From last time: name the yellow non-metal powder used in some medicines and to make rubber stronger.
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: wo peela non-metal powder kaunsa hai jo kuch dawaiyon mein aur rubber ko mazboot banane mein use hota hai?
served.answer: Sulphur.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
served.prompt: Is melting ghee a physical or a chemical change? Why?
served.prompt_hi: Ghee ka pighalna physical badlav hai ya chemical? Kyon?
served.answer: Physical: it is still ghee, only changed from solid to liquid, and it becomes solid again when it cools.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
served.prompt: Which change can NOT be reversed to get the original substance back?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa badlav ulta karke original cheez waapas nahi la sakte?
served.answer: Making curd from milk

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can distinguish physical and chemical changes using evidence (new substance, heat, gas, colour)
served.prompt: From last time: when water freezes in the freezer, is it a physical or a chemical change?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab freezer mein paani jamta hai, toh ye physical badlav hai ya chemical?
served.answer: Physical: it is still water, only in the solid state.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
served.prompt: Which gas from the air is needed for burning?
served.prompt_hi: Jalne ke liye hawa ki kaunsi gas zaroori hai?
served.answer: Oxygen.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
served.prompt: A candle burns for an hour and becomes much shorter. Where did most of the wax go?
served.prompt_hi: Ek mombatti ek ghante jalti hai aur bahut chhoti ho jaati hai. Zyadatar wax kahaan gaya?
served.answer: It turned into gases such as carbon dioxide and water vapour that went into the air

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
outcomes: Learner can describe combustion and rusting as chemical changes that need oxygen
served.prompt: From last time: is burning a physical or a chemical change, and what does it give out?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jalna physical badlav hai ya chemical, aur isse kya nikalta hai?
served.answer: A chemical change; it gives out heat and light, and makes new substances such as carbon dioxide.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
served.topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
served.prompt: What is weathering? Give one cause of it.
served.prompt_hi: Weathering kya hai? Iska ek kaaran batao.
served.answer: Weathering is the slow breaking down of rocks where they are; causes include heating and cooling, water freezing in cracks, plant roots growing into cracks, and rainwater.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
served.topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
served.prompt: Which is true about the rocks of the Himalayas?
served.prompt_hi: Himalaya ki chattanon ke baare mein kya sach hai?
served.answer: They are slowly being broken down and worn away by ice, water and wind

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Changes Around Us: Physical and Chemical
served.topic: Slow natural changes: weathering and erosion
outcomes: Learner can explain weathering and erosion as slow changes that shape the land
served.prompt: From last time: name one thing that can break rocks without any people being involved.
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi cheez batao jo bina kisi insaan ke chattanon ko tod sakti hai.
served.answer: Any one of: water freezing in cracks, plant roots, heating and cooling, rainwater.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
served.prompt: What is the stage of life between childhood and adulthood called, and roughly what ages does it cover?
served.prompt_hi: Bachpan aur badappan ke beech ke jeevan ke daur ko kya kehte hain, aur ye lagbhag kis umar tak hota hai?
served.answer: Adolescence; roughly from 10 to 19 years of age.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
served.prompt: Ravi is 13 and has grown a lot this year. His friend Sunil, also 13, has hardly grown. What is most likely true?
served.prompt_hi: Ravi 13 saal ka hai aur is saal bahut lamba ho gaya. Uska dost Sunil bhi 13 ka hai par zyada nahi badha. Sabse zyada kya sach hone ki sambhavna hai?
served.answer: Changes start at different ages; Sunil's growth spurt may simply come later

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can describe physical changes during adolescence and that they happen at different ages for different people
served.prompt: From last time: what are the chemical messengers that bring about the changes of adolescence called?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: adolescence ke badlav laane wale chemical messengers ko kya kehte hain?
served.answer: Hormones.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
served.prompt: Name two emotional changes that many people notice during adolescence.
served.prompt_hi: Do aise bhaavnaatmak badlav batao jo bahut log adolescence mein mehsoos karte hain.
served.answer: Any two of: quick mood changes, wanting more independence, caring more about looks, caring more about what friends think, feeling more sensitive or worried.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
served.prompt: Asha has a question about the changes in her body but feels embarrassed. What is the best thing to do?
served.prompt_hi: Asha ke paas apne shareer mein ho rahe badlavon ke baare mein ek sawaal hai par use sharm aa rahi hai. Sabse accha kya hoga?
served.answer: Ask a trusted adult like her mother, a teacher or a doctor, or drop it in the class question box

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can identify emotional changes in adolescence and trusted people to talk to
served.prompt: Why is it normal to have strong or changing feelings during adolescence?
served.prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan tez ya badalti bhaavnaayein hona normal kyon hai?
served.answer: Hormones and many big changes in the body, school and friendships all happen at once, and the brain is still developing; everyone goes through this.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
served.prompt: Why do adolescents need more protein and calcium in their diet?
served.prompt_hi: Adolescents ko apne khaane mein zyada protein aur calcium ki zaroorat kyon hoti hai?
served.answer: For fast growth: protein builds muscles and other body parts, and calcium builds strong bones and teeth.

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
served.prompt: Pooja wants to be fit and stops eating breakfast. What is most likely to happen?
served.prompt_hi: Pooja fit rehna chahti hai aur nashta karna band kar deti hai. Sabse zyada kya hone ki sambhavna hai?
served.answer: She will feel tired and find it hard to concentrate; a healthy breakfast and exercise work better

served.subject: science
served.chapter: Adolescence: A Stage of Growth and Change
outcomes: Learner can plan diet, hygiene and physical activity routines suited to adolescence
served.prompt: Predict which breakfast will keep you full and active longer until lunch: a packet of chips with a cola, or poha with peanuts and a glass of milk.
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo kaunsa nashta tumhe lunch tak zyada der bhara aur active rakhega: chips ka packet aur cola, ya moongfali wala poha aur ek glass doodh.
served.answer: Poha with peanuts and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein and some fat that release energy steadily; chips and cola give a quick sugar rush, little nutrition, and hunger again soon.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
served.prompt: In which direction does heat always flow between two objects?
served.prompt_hi: Do cheezon ke beech garmi hamesha kis disha mein behti hai?
served.answer: From the hotter object to the colder one.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
served.prompt: One ice cube is wrapped in a woollen sweater and another is left unwrapped on a plate in the same room. What happens?
served.prompt_hi: Ek barf ke tukde ko oon ke sweater mein lapeta gaya aur doosre ko usi kamre mein plate pe khula chhoda gaya. Kya hoga?
served.answer: The wrapped one melts more slowly because wool traps air and slows the heat flowing in from the room

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain conduction and identify good and poor conductors of heat
served.prompt: Draw a steel rod with one end dipped in a pot of hot water and three markers stuck along its length. Show with arrows how heat moves, and number the markers in the order they would warm up.
served.prompt_hi: Ek steel ki rod banao jiska ek sira garam paani ke bartan mein dooba ho aur uski lambaai pe teen marker lage hon. Teer se dikhao ki garmi kaise chalti hai, aur markers ko us kram mein number do jis kram mein wo garam honge.
served.answer: Arrows go from the end in the hot water along the rod towards the dry end. The marker nearest the hot water warms first (1), then the middle one (2), then the farthest one (3).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
served.prompt: What is the transfer of heat by the movement of a heated liquid or gas called?
served.prompt_hi: Garam liquid ya gas ke chalne se garmi ke pahunchne ko kya kehte hain?
served.answer: Convection.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
served.prompt: You sit beside a room heater, not above it, and feel warm. How does the heat reach you?
served.prompt_hi: Tum room heater ke bagal mein baithe ho, upar nahi, aur garmi mehsoos hoti hai. Garmi tum tak kaise pahunchi?
served.answer: Heat flows from hot to cold in all directions; here it reaches you mostly by radiation

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain convection in liquids and air and the land and sea breeze
served.prompt: Freeze water with a few drops of food colour to make a coloured ice cube. Gently drop it into a clear glass of warm water. Predict where the coloured water will go as the ice melts.
served.prompt_hi: Paani mein khaane ka rang daal ke rangeen barf ka tukda jamaao. Use dheere se garam paani ke saaf glass mein daalo. Guess karo barf pighalne pe rangeen paani kahaan jaayega.
served.answer: The cold coloured water sinks to the bottom, because cold water is heavier (denser) than warm water; the warm water stays above. This sinking and rising is convection.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
served.prompt: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
served.prompt_hi: Sun ki garmi Earth tak kaise pahunchti hai?
served.answer: By radiation.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
served.prompt: Between the Sun and the Earth there is almost empty space. How does the Sun's heat reach us?
served.prompt_hi: Sun aur Earth ke beech lagbhag khaali space hai. Sun ki garmi hum tak kaise pahunchti hai?
served.answer: By radiation, which needs no material to travel through

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how heat from the Sun reaches us and why light colours are worn in summer
served.prompt: From last time: which way of heat transfer can work through empty space?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi pahunchne ka kaunsa tareeka khaali space mein bhi kaam karta hai?
served.answer: Radiation.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
served.prompt: Name the main steps of the water cycle.
served.prompt_hi: Jal chakra ke mukhya kadam batao.
served.answer: Evaporation (and transpiration from plants), condensation into clouds, precipitation as rain, snow or hail, and collection in rivers, seas and groundwater.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
served.prompt: If you could see the groundwater under a village, what would it mostly look like?
served.prompt_hi: Agar tum gaon ke neeche ka groundwater dekh sakte, toh wo zyadatar kaisa dikhta?
served.answer: Water filling tiny gaps between grains of sand and gravel and cracks in rock, like water in a sponge

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain the water cycle including infiltration and groundwater
served.prompt: Only with an adult beside you, and standing well back (never put your hand or face near the steam): look at a boiling kettle on the stove. Compare the clear gap right at the spout with the white mist a little above it. Which one is like a cloud, and why?
served.prompt_hi: Sirf kisi bade ke saath, aur door khade hokar (bhaap ke paas haath ya chehra bilkul mat le jaana): stove pe ubalti ketli ko dekho. Tonti ke theek paas ke saaf hisse aur thoda upar wali safed dhundh ki tulna karo. Inmein se baadal jaisa kaun hai, aur kyon?
served.answer: The white mist is like a cloud: it is made of tiny water droplets that formed when the invisible water vapour cooled and condensed. The clear part right at the spout is water vapour gas, which we cannot see.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
served.prompt: What is the SI unit of time?
served.prompt_hi: Samay ki SI unit kya hai?
served.answer: The second (s).

served.subject: science
served.topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
served.prompt: Two pendulums have the same thread length; one has a light eraser as its bob and the other a heavy key. Which has the shorter time period?
served.prompt_hi: Do pendulum ki dhaage ki lambaai barabar hai; ek mein halka rubber laga hai aur doosre mein bhaari chaabi. Kiska time period chhota hoga?
served.answer: Both have about the same time period, because the bob's mass does not change it

served.subject: science
served.topic: Measuring time and the simple pendulum
outcomes: Learner can measure the time period of a pendulum and state the SI unit of time
served.prompt: From last time: what was the giant sundial at Jantar Mantar used for?
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Jantar Mantar ki vishaal sundial kis kaam aati thi?
served.answer: To tell the time of day from the position of its shadow (it is called the Samrat Yantra).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can calculate speed from distance and time and compare speeds
served.prompt: From last time: write the formula for speed and its SI unit.
served.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: speed ka formula aur uski SI unit likho.
served.answer: Speed = distance ÷ time; the SI unit is metres per second (m/s).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can calculate speed from distance and time and compare speeds
served.prompt: A bus travels 120 km in 3 hours. A car travels 100 km in 2 hours. Which is faster?
served.prompt_hi: Ek bus 3 ghante mein 120 km jaati hai. Ek car 2 ghante mein 100 km jaati hai. Kaun tez hai?
served.answer: The car: 50 km/h is faster than the bus's 40 km/h

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can calculate speed from distance and time and compare speeds
served.prompt: Why does a speedometer reading of 50 km/h NOT mean the car has travelled 50 km?
served.prompt_hi: Speedometer pe 50 km/h dikhne ka matlab ye kyon NAHI hai ki car 50 km chal chuki hai?
served.answer: It shows how fast the car is going at that moment, meaning it would cover 50 km in one hour at that speed; the distance already travelled is shown by the odometer.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can distinguish uniform and non-uniform motion from data
served.prompt: What is uniform linear motion?
served.prompt_hi: Uniform linear motion kya hoti hai?
served.answer: Motion along a straight line in which an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed stays the same.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can distinguish uniform and non-uniform motion from data
served.prompt: An auto keeps moving for 10 minutes without stopping, but it speeds up and slows down in traffic. Is its motion uniform?
served.prompt_hi: Ek auto 10 minute bina ruke chalta hai, par traffic mein tez aur dheere hota rehta hai. Kya uski gati ek-samaan (uniform) hai?
served.answer: No, because it covers different distances in equal intervals of time

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can distinguish uniform and non-uniform motion from data
served.prompt: A car's total distance from the start after each minute is 1 km, 2 km, 3 km and 4 km. Is its motion uniform? How do you know?
served.prompt_hi: Ek car ki shuruaat se kul doori har minute ke baad 1 km, 2 km, 3 km aur 4 km hai. Kya uski gati uniform hai? Kaise pata?
served.answer: Yes, it covers 1 km in every minute, which is equal distances in equal times.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe the path of food through the digestive system and what happens at each stage
served.prompt: Put these in the order food travels: stomach, mouth, large intestine, food pipe, small intestine.
served.prompt_hi: Inhe us order mein lagaao jismein khaana chalta hai: stomach, munh, large intestine, food pipe, small intestine.
served.answer: Mouth, food pipe (oesophagus), stomach, small intestine, large intestine (then rectum and anus).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe the path of food through the digestive system and what happens at each stage
served.prompt: You chew a piece of plain roti for a full minute without swallowing. It starts tasting slightly sweet. Why?
served.prompt_hi: Tum saadi roti ka tukda ek minute tak chabaate ho bina nigle. Woh thoda meetha lagne lagta hai. Kyun?
served.answer: Saliva starts changing the starch in roti into sugar

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe the path of food through the digestive system and what happens at each stage
served.prompt: Astronauts in space, with no 'down', can still swallow food and it reaches their stomach. Predict how, before you hear the answer.
served.prompt_hi: Space mein astronauts ke liye koi 'neeche' nahi hota, phir bhi woh khaana nigal lete hain aur woh pet tak pahunchta hai. Jawaab sunne se pehle guess karo kaise.
served.answer: The walls of the food pipe squeeze in waves and push the food along, so food moves even without gravity.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can compare how different animals take in and digest food
served.prompt: Match each animal to how it takes in food: butterfly, snake, cow, eagle. Ways: (a) sucks nectar (b) swallows prey whole (c) grinds grass (d) tears flesh with a hooked beak.
served.prompt_hi: Har jaanvar ko uske khaane ke tareeke se milaao: titli, saanp, gaay, cheel. Tareeke: (a) nectar choosti hai (b) shikaar poora nigalta hai (c) ghaas peesti hai (d) mudi chonch se maans faadti hai.
served.answer: Butterfly (a), snake (b), cow (c), eagle (d).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can compare how different animals take in and digest food
served.prompt: An amoeba is a single cell with no mouth or stomach. How does it eat?
served.prompt_hi: Amoeba ek single cell hai, na munh hai na pet. Woh khaata kaise hai?
served.answer: It surrounds food with pseudopodia, traps it in a food vacuole and digests it there

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can compare how different animals take in and digest food
served.prompt: Compare how a human and a snake deal with a big piece of food.
served.prompt_hi: Insaan aur saanp bade khaane ke tukde ke saath kya karte hain, compare karo.
served.answer: A human cuts and chews food into small pieces using teeth before swallowing; a snake swallows prey whole, stretching its jaws, and digests it slowly in its body.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain breathing and respiration and how different animals breathe
served.prompt: Say whether each is breathing or respiration: (a) your chest rises and falls (b) a muscle cell breaks down glucose to get energy (c) air goes in through your nose.
served.prompt_hi: Batao har ek breathing hai ya respiration: (a) chhaati upar-neeche hoti hai (b) muscle cell glucose todke energy leta hai (c) hawa naak se andar jaati hai.
served.answer: (a) breathing (b) respiration (c) breathing.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain breathing and respiration and how different animals breathe
served.prompt: Where does respiration (using oxygen to release energy from food) actually take place?
served.prompt_hi: Respiration (oxygen se khaane mein se energy nikaalna) asal mein kahaan hota hai?
served.answer: In every cell of the body

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain breathing and respiration and how different animals breathe
served.prompt: Why do we need oxygen at all? What would stop if oxygen did not reach our cells?
served.prompt_hi: Humein oxygen ki zaroorat hi kyun hai? Agar oxygen cells tak na pahunche toh kya ruk jaayega?
served.answer: Cells use oxygen to break down food (glucose) and release the energy needed for every activity; without it, cells cannot release enough energy and stop working.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain that plants make food in leaves using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
served.prompt: A famous experiment (van Helmont, about 400 years ago): a willow sapling of about 2.3 kg was grown in a tub of 90 kg of dried soil for five years, given only water. It grew to about 77 kg. Predict how much soil was lost: about 74 kg, about 7 kg, or only about 57 grams?
served.prompt_hi: Ek mashhoor experiment (van Helmont, lagbhag 400 saal pehle): lagbhag 2.3 kg ka willow ka paudha 90 kg sukhi mitti ke tub mein paanch saal tak ugaaya gaya, sirf paani diya gaya. Woh lagbhag 77 kg ka ho gaya. Guess karo kitni mitti kam hui: lagbhag 74 kg, 7 kg, ya sirf 57 gram?
served.answer: Only about 57 grams; almost none of the tree's mass came from the soil. It came from carbon dioxide in the air and water, through photosynthesis.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain that plants make food in leaves using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
served.prompt: A small plant is grown in a pot of soil for five years and becomes a large plant. The soil is weighed before and after. What would you expect?
served.prompt_hi: Ek chhota paudha gamle ki mitti mein paanch saal ugaaya gaya aur bada ho gaya. Mitti ko pehle aur baad mein taula gaya. Kya ummeed karoge?
served.answer: The soil lost only a very little mass; the plant's mass came mainly from air (carbon dioxide) and water

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain that plants make food in leaves using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide
served.prompt: If soil does not give plants food, why do farmers add manure and fertilisers?
served.prompt_hi: Agar mitti paudhon ko khaana nahi deti, toh kisaan khaad aur fertiliser kyun daalte hain?
served.answer: They supply minerals such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium that plants need in small amounts to grow healthily and make proteins and chlorophyll; the food itself is made by photosynthesis.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe stomata and gas exchange in leaves
served.prompt: What are stomata, and where are most of them found on a leaf?
served.prompt_hi: Stomata kya hote hain, aur patte pe zyada-tar kahaan milte hain?
served.answer: Tiny pores in the leaf surface, each controlled by two guard cells; most are on the lower surface of leaves.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe stomata and gas exchange in leaves
served.prompt: A leaf is kept in complete darkness overnight. Which gas will it take in through its stomata?
served.prompt_hi: Ek patta poori raat andhere mein rakha hai. Woh stomata se kaunsi gas andar lega?
served.answer: Oxygen, for respiration

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe stomata and gas exchange in leaves
served.prompt: What do guard cells do?
served.prompt_hi: Guard cells kya kaam karte hain?
served.answer: They open and close each stoma, controlling how much gas enters and leaves and how much water vapour is lost.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Transport of water and food in plants
outcomes: Learner can explain how water and minerals move up and food moves to all parts
served.prompt: Which tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa tissue paani aur minerals ko jadon se patton tak le jaata hai?
served.answer: Xylem.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Transport of water and food in plants
outcomes: Learner can explain how water and minerals move up and food moves to all parts
served.prompt: A white flower's stalk is placed in water coloured with food colour. After some hours the petals show the colour. In which direction did the water move?
served.prompt_hi: Safed phool ki daandi ko food colour wale paani mein rakha. Kuch ghanton baad pankhudiyon mein rang aa gaya. Paani kis disha mein chala?
served.answer: Up the stem from the water to the petals

served.subject: science
served.topic: Transport of water and food in plants
outcomes: Learner can explain how water and minerals move up and food moves to all parts
served.prompt: Put a white flower (or a stalk of celery) in a glass of water with a few drops of food colour. Before waiting, predict what you will see after a few hours, and where the colour will appear first.
served.prompt_hi: Ek safed phool (ya celery ki daandi) ko kuch boond food colour wale paani ke glass mein rakho. Intezaar se pehle guess karo kuch ghanton mein kya dikhega, aur rang sabse pehle kahaan aayega.
served.answer: The colour rises up the stem and appears in the petals (or leaf veins), first near the bottom and then at the top, because water travels up through the xylem.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify sources as luminous or non-luminous and materials as transparent, translucent or opaque
served.prompt: Sort into luminous and non-luminous: Sun, Moon, candle flame, mirror, firefly, notebook.
served.prompt_hi: Luminous aur non-luminous mein baanto: Sooraj, Chaand, mombatti ki lau, sheesha, jugnu, copy.
served.answer: Luminous: Sun, candle flame, firefly. Non-luminous: Moon, mirror, notebook.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify sources as luminous or non-luminous and materials as transparent, translucent or opaque
served.prompt: On a full moon night the Moon looks very bright. Where does its light come from?
served.prompt_hi: Poornima ki raat chaand bahut chamakdaar dikhta hai. Uski roshni kahaan se aati hai?
served.answer: Sunlight falls on the Moon and is reflected towards Earth

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can classify sources as luminous or non-luminous and materials as transparent, translucent or opaque
served.prompt: From memory: give two examples of luminous objects.
served.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: do luminous cheezon ke naam.
served.answer: Any two: Sun, stars, candle flame, lit bulb, firefly, glowing torch.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how shadows form because light travels in straight lines
served.prompt: What three things are needed to see a shadow?
served.prompt_hi: Parchhaai dekhne ke liye kaunsi teen cheezein chahiye?
served.answer: A source of light, an opaque object and a screen (surface) for the shadow to fall on.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how shadows form because light travels in straight lines
served.prompt: You stand between a lamp and a wall. What do you see on the wall?
served.prompt_hi: Tum lamp aur deewar ke beech khade ho. Deewar pe kya dikhta hai?
served.answer: A dark outline of your shape, because your body blocks the light

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how shadows form because light travels in straight lines
served.prompt: From memory: can a transparent sheet of glass make a dark shadow? Why or why not?
served.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: kya saaf kaanch ki sheet kaali parchhaai bana sakti hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
served.answer: No (at most a very faint one), because it lets almost all light pass through; dark shadows need opaque objects.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe reflection and images in a plane mirror (lateral inversion)
served.prompt: Why do you see your face clearly in a steel plate but not in a wooden table, though light falls on both?
served.prompt_hi: Steel ki plate mein chehra saaf dikhta hai par lakdi ki mez mein nahi, jabki roshni dono pe padti hai. Kyun?
served.answer: The polished steel is smooth and shiny, so it reflects light regularly in one direction and forms a clear image; the rough wood scatters light in many directions, so no clear image forms.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe reflection and images in a plane mirror (lateral inversion)
served.prompt: You stand 2 metres in front of a big mirror. How far from you does your image appear to be?
served.prompt_hi: Tum ek bade sheeshe se 2 meter door khade ho. Tumhari image tumse kitni door dikhti hai?
served.answer: 4 metres: 2 metres behind the mirror, so 2 + 2 from you

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can describe reflection and images in a plane mirror (lateral inversion)
served.prompt: List three features of the image formed by a plane mirror.
served.prompt_hi: Plane mirror se bani image ki teen visheshtaayein batao.
served.answer: Any three: upright; same size as the object; as far behind the mirror as the object is in front; laterally inverted; cannot be caught on a screen.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can make a pinhole camera or periscope and explain how it works
served.prompt: You make a pinhole camera and point it at a bright lit bulb in a dark room (never at the Sun). Before you look, predict how the bulb's image will appear on the screen.
served.prompt_hi: Tumne pinhole camera banaaya aur andhere kamre mein jalte bulb ki taraf kiya (Sooraj ki taraf kabhi nahi). Dekhne se pehle guess karo screen pe bulb ki image kaisi dikhegi.
served.answer: Small and upside down (inverted), because light travels in straight lines through the pinhole.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can make a pinhole camera or periscope and explain how it works
served.prompt: Through a pinhole camera you view a tall tree. How does the tree appear on the butter-paper screen?
served.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera se tum ek lamba ped dekhte ho. Butter paper screen pe ped kaisa dikhta hai?
served.answer: Upside down, because rays from the top go straight through the hole to the bottom of the screen

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can make a pinhole camera or periscope and explain how it works
served.prompt: Predict: if you make the pinhole bigger, how will the image change?
served.prompt_hi: Guess karo: pinhole bada karne pe image kaise badlegi?
served.answer: It becomes brighter but blurred, because a big hole is like many small holes each making an image, and these overlap.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Rotation and revolution of the Earth
outcomes: Learner can explain day-night by rotation and the year by revolution
served.prompt: How long does the Earth take to rotate once on its axis, and in which direction does it rotate?
served.prompt_hi: Earth apni axis pe ek baar ghoomne mein kitna samay leti hai, aur kis disha mein ghoomti hai?
served.answer: About 24 hours, from west to east.

served.subject: science
served.topic: Rotation and revolution of the Earth
outcomes: Learner can explain day-night by rotation and the year by revolution
served.prompt: Why do we have day and night?
served.prompt_hi: Din aur raat kyun hote hain?
served.answer: The Earth spins on its axis, so each place faces the Sun for part of the day and faces away for the rest

served.subject: science
served.topic: Rotation and revolution of the Earth
outcomes: Learner can explain day-night by rotation and the year by revolution
served.prompt: In a dark room, shine a torch on a globe (or a ball with a dot marking India). Before you turn it, predict: if you spin the globe slowly from west to east, from which direction will the 'Sun' first appear for the dot?
served.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein globe (ya ball jispe India ka nishaan ho) pe torch daalo. Ghumaane se pehle guess karo: globe ko pashchim se poorab dheere ghumaane pe, nishaan ke liye 'Sooraj' kis disha se pehle dikhega?
served.answer: From the east: the dot turns into the light from the eastern side, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the east.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain seasons by the tilt of the Earth’s axis
served.prompt: By about how many degrees is the Earth's axis tilted?
served.prompt_hi: Earth ki axis lagbhag kitne degree jhuki hui hai?
served.answer: About 23.5° (from the perpendicular to its orbit).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain seasons by the tilt of the Earth’s axis
served.prompt: In early January the Earth is at its closest to the Sun. What season is it then in India?
served.prompt_hi: January ki shuruaat mein Earth Sooraj ke sabse paas hoti hai. Tab India mein kaunsa mausam hota hai?
served.answer: Winter, so distance cannot be the cause of seasons

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain seasons by the tilt of the Earth’s axis
served.prompt: A website says: 'We have summer because the Earth moves closer to the Sun.' Give two pieces of evidence that this is wrong.
served.prompt_hi: Ek website kehti hai: 'Garmi isliye hoti hai kyunki Earth Sooraj ke paas aa jaati hai.' Do saboot do ki ye galat hai.
served.answer: 1) The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during northern winter. 2) The two hemispheres have opposite seasons at the same time, which distance cannot explain since both are at the same distance.

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how solar and lunar eclipses occur and how to view them safely
served.prompt: On which day can a solar eclipse happen: new moon (amavasya) or full moon (purnima)?
served.prompt_hi: Surya grahan kis din ho sakta hai: amaavasya ya poornima?
served.answer: New moon (amavasya).

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how solar and lunar eclipses occur and how to view them safely
served.prompt: There is a full moon about every month. Why is there not a lunar eclipse every month?
served.prompt_hi: Lagbhag har mahine poornima hoti hai. Toh har mahine chandra grahan kyun nahi hota?
served.answer: Because the Moon's orbit is tilted, so usually the Moon passes above or below the Earth's shadow

served.subject: science
outcomes: Learner can explain how solar and lunar eclipses occur and how to view them safely
served.prompt: In a dark room, put a torch (Sun), a small ball (Moon) and a big ball (Earth) in a straight line with the small ball in the middle. Before you look, predict what falls on the big ball.
served.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein torch (Sooraj), chhoti ball (Chaand) aur badi ball (Earth) ek seedhi line mein rakho, chhoti ball beech mein. Dekhne se pehle guess karo badi ball pe kya padega.
served.answer: The small ball's shadow falls on a small part of the big ball: this models a solar eclipse, seen only from the places where the Moon's shadow falls.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: a girl’s questions and her wish to learn)

served.prompt: Read: 'Every evening, Meenu sat by the river while her brothers did homework. "Why can't I go to school too?" she asked. The river seemed to whisper, "Keep asking. Every question is a small step." Next morning, Meenu walked to the headmaster's door.' Where did Meenu sit every evening?
served.prompt_hi: Kahani suno. Meenu har shaam kahaan baithti thi?
served.answer: By the river

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: a girl’s questions and her wish to learn)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Which question is correct: 'Why you are sad, Meenu?' or 'Why are you sad, Meenu?'
served.prompt_hi: Dono suno — 'Why you are sad?' aur 'Why are you sad?'. English mein sawaal kaunsa sahi banta hai?
served.answer: Why are you sad, Meenu?

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: a girl’s questions and her wish to learn)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'Every evening, Meenu sat by the river while her brothers did homework. "Why can't I go to school too?" she asked. The river seemed to whisper, "Keep asking. Every question is a small step." Next morning, Meenu walked to the headmaster's door.' What do you think Meenu will say to the headmaster?
served.prompt_hi: Agla kya hoga? Headmaster ke darwaaze par Meenu kya bolegi?
served.answer: She will ask if she can join the school and learn to read

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: perseverance)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read these lines aloud and clap on the strong beats: 'The rope was high, my arms were sore, / I fell, I rose, I tried once more.' Which words get the strongest beat at the end of each line?
served.prompt_hi: Ye do lines taali ke saath padho. Har line ke aakhir mein kis word par sabse zor aata hai?
served.answer: sore and more

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: perseverance)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Which is correct: 'If you try again, you will succeed' or 'If you will try again, you will succeed'?
served.prompt_hi: Kaunsa sahi hai? 'If you try again, you will succeed' ya 'If you will try again, you will succeed'?
served.answer: If you try again, you will succeed.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: perseverance)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: What is a refrain in a poem?
served.prompt_hi: Kavita mein 'refrain' kya hota hai?
served.answer: A line or phrase that is repeated, often at the end of each stanza

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can identify the main ideas and supporting details of the text and respond in writing (theme: valuing our senses (Helen Keller))
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'If I could see for just three days, I would first look at the faces of the people I love. I would walk in a garden at sunrise and watch the colours change. At night, I would gaze at the stars and try to hold them in my memory. Those of us who can see often forget how lucky we are.' What would the writer look at first?
served.prompt_hi: Passage suno. Writer sabse pehle kya dekhna chahti hai?
served.answer: The faces of the people she loves

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can identify the main ideas and supporting details of the text and respond in writing (theme: valuing our senses (Helen Keller))
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Helen Keller imagines having sight. Which is correct: 'If I had three days to see, I would look at my friends' faces' or 'If I have three days to see, I would look at my friends' faces'?
served.prompt_hi: Yeh kalpana hai, sach nahi. To kaunsa sahi: 'If I had three days…, I would…' ya 'If I have three days…, I would…'?
served.answer: If I had three days to see, I would look at my friends' faces.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can identify the main ideas and supporting details of the text and respond in writing (theme: valuing our senses (Helen Keller))
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'If I could see for just three days, I would first look at the faces of the people I love. I would walk in a garden at sunrise and watch the colours change. At night, I would gaze at the stars and try to hold them in my memory. Those of us who can see often forget how lucky we are.' Which sentence gives the main idea of the passage?
served.prompt_hi: Inmein se kaunsi line poore passage ka main idea batati hai?
served.answer: Those of us who can see often forget how lucky we are.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: communicating with animals)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'Doctor Ramu liked animals more than people. One day his parrot Mitthu said, "Animals talk too. A dog talks with its tail, a cow with its ears." Soon the doctor understood them all, and sick animals came from far away to his clinic.' Who helped Doctor Ramu understand the animals?
served.prompt_hi: Kahani suno. Doctor Ramu ko jaanwaron ki baat samajhne mein kisne madad ki?
served.answer: His parrot Mitthu

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: communicating with animals)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Which is correct: 'The parrot told the doctor that dogs talk with their tails' or 'The parrot told that dogs talk with their tails'?
served.prompt_hi: 'Told' ke baad kisko bataya, yeh zaroori hai kya? Kaunsa sahi hai?
served.answer: The parrot told the doctor that dogs talk with their tails.

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can summarise the story, infer characters’ feelings and motives, and discuss its message (theme: communicating with animals)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: A cow comes to the clinic holding one ear down and swishing her tail slowly. Using the parrot's idea, what will the doctor do first?
served.prompt_hi: Ek gaay aayi, ek kaan neeche, poonch dheere hilaati. Doctor pehle kya karega?
served.answer: He will watch her ears and tail to understand how she feels and what hurts

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: nonsense humour)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'There lived a man in Ludhiana / Who wore his shoes upon his ears; / He ate his soup with a banana / And laughed so hard he cried for years.' Where did the man wear his shoes?
served.prompt_hi: Kavita suno. Aadmi joote kahaan pehenta tha?
served.answer: Upon his ears

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: nonsense humour)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Why does the poet say the man wore his shoes upon his ears?
served.prompt_hi: Kavi kehte hain aadmi kaanon par joote pehenta tha. Aisa kyun likha?
served.answer: To make us laugh with something impossible

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can read the poem aloud, explain its central idea and identify imagery or rhyme (theme: nonsense humour)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: In a nonsense poem, the funny man gets ready for bed. What might he do? Give one silly idea that fits a nonsense poem.
served.prompt_hi: Funny man so raha hai. Nonsense kavita mein woh kya ulta-pulta karega?
served.answer: Something impossible or upside-down, for example sleeping on the ceiling or using a frying pan as a pillow

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can perform scenes from the play in roles and discuss how dialogue builds the plot (theme: humour and politeness with guests)
Learner can use new vocabulary and grammar items from the lesson in speaking and writing
served.prompt: Read: 'MOTHER: Raju, Mrs Sharma is coming. Be polite and say the right thing. (The bell rings.) RAJU: Hello, aunty! Mummy says you talk too much, so I'll keep it short. MOTHER: (turning red) Raju! Would you like some tea, Mrs Sharma?' What did Mother tell Raju before the guest came?
served.prompt_hi: Mehmaan aane se pehle Mummy ne Raju ko kya kaha?
served.answer: To be polite and say the right thing

served.subject: english
outcomes: Learner can perform scenes from the play in roles and discuss how dialogue builds the plot (theme: humour and politeness with guests)

served.topic: From the Rulers to the Ruled: Types of Governments
outcomes: Learner can compare monarchy, democracy, dictatorship and other forms of government
served.prompt: What would happen in a cricket match with no rules and no umpire? How is that like a country without a government?
served.prompt_hi: Bina niyam aur bina umpire ke cricket match mein kya hoga? Yeh bina sarkaar wale desh jaisa kaise hai?
served.answer: Players would argue, the strongest would get their way and the game might break down; similarly, without a government and rules, there would be no fair way to decide, settle quarrels or keep people safe.

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
served.topic: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
outcomes: Learner can explain why a constitution is needed and describe key ideas in the Preamble
served.prompt: Why does a country need a constitution?
served.prompt_hi: Ek desh ko samvidhan ki zaroorat kyun hoti hai?
served.answer: It is the basic rulebook: it sets up the government and limits its powers, lists citizens' rights and duties, and gives a fair framework that all other laws must follow — so that power is not misused.

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
served.topic: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
outcomes: Learner can explain why a constitution is needed and describe key ideas in the Preamble
served.prompt: Can India's Constitution be changed?
served.prompt_hi: Kya Bharat ka Samvidhan badla ja sakta hai?
served.answer: Yes — through amendments passed by a special process in Parliament; it has been amended more than 100 times

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
served.topic: The Constitution of India — An Introduction
outcomes: Learner can explain why a constitution is needed and describe key ideas in the Preamble
served.prompt: When was the Constitution adopted, and when did it come into force? Which days do we celebrate for each?
served.prompt_hi: Samvidhan kab apnaya gaya aur kab laagu hua? Har ek ke liye hum kaunsa din manaate hain?
served.answer: Adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day / Samvidhan Divas); came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain the problems of barter and how money evolved, including digital payments
served.prompt: What is barter?
served.prompt_hi: Vastu-vinimay (barter) kya hai?
served.answer: Exchanging goods or services directly for other goods or services, without using money.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain the problems of barter and how money evolved, including digital payments
served.prompt: The paper in a ₹500 note costs only a few rupees to make. Why can you buy ₹500 worth of things with it?
served.prompt_hi: ₹500 ke note ka kaagaz banane mein sirf kuch rupaye lagte hain. Phir bhi usse ₹500 ki cheezein kyun khareedi ja sakti hain?
served.answer: Because everyone trusts it and the law, backed by the RBI and the government, makes it acceptable for payment

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain the problems of barter and how money evolved, including digital payments
served.prompt: A weaver wants rice, the rice farmer wants shoes, and the cobbler wants cloth. Explain the problem and show how they could still barter.
served.prompt_hi: Bunkar ko chaawal chahiye, chaawal wale kisaan ko joote chahiye, aur mochi ko kapda chahiye. Mushkil samjhao aur batao ki phir bhi ve barter kaise kar sakte hain.
served.answer: No pair has a double coincidence of wants. They can still trade in a circle: the weaver gives cloth to the cobbler, the cobbler gives shoes to the farmer, and the farmer gives rice to the weaver — but this needs all three to meet and agree, which is hard.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe different kinds of markets and how buyers and sellers interact
served.prompt: Name four different kinds of markets.
served.prompt_hi: Chaar alag tarah ke bazaaron ke naam batao.
served.answer: Weekly haat, neighbourhood shops, wholesale mandi, shopping mall, online market (any four).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe different kinds of markets and how buyers and sellers interact
served.prompt: Heavy rains destroy many tomato crops in a state. What will most likely happen to tomato prices in the markets there?
served.prompt_hi: Ek rajya mein bhaari baarish se tamatar ki bahut fasal barbaad ho jaati hai. Wahan ke bazaaron mein tamatar ke daam ka kya hoga?
served.answer: They will rise, because there are fewer tomatoes but people still want them

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe different kinds of markets and how buyers and sellers interact
served.prompt: Is an online shopping app a market? Explain.
served.prompt_hi: Kya online shopping app ek bazaar hai? Samjhao.
served.answer: Yes: a market is wherever buyers and sellers meet to exchange goods or services; online, they meet through an app or website instead of a physical place.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can trace the history of farming in India and describe crops, seasons and challenges faced by farmers today
served.prompt: Name one of the earliest farming sites in the subcontinent, about when people farmed there, and two things they grew.
served.prompt_hi: Upmahadweep ki sabse puraani kheti wali jagahon mein se ek ka naam batao, wahan lagbhag kab kheti hoti thi, aur ve kya do cheezein ugaate the.
served.answer: Mehrgarh (in present-day Pakistan), around 7000 BCE; wheat and barley (they also kept cattle, sheep and goats).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can trace the history of farming in India and describe crops, seasons and challenges faced by farmers today
served.prompt: Which of these is a rabi crop, sown around October–December and harvested in spring?
served.prompt_hi: Inme se kaunsi rabi fasal hai, jo October–December ke aas-paas boyi jaati hai aur vasant mein kaati jaati hai?
served.answer: Wheat

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can trace the history of farming in India and describe crops, seasons and challenges faced by farmers today
served.prompt: Put in order: the Green Revolution; farming begins at Mehrgarh; Kallanai built on the Kaveri; Harappan farmers grow cotton.
served.prompt_hi: Kram mein lagao: Hari Kranti (Green Revolution); Mehrgarh mein kheti shuru; Kaveri par Kallanai bana; Harappa ke kisaan kapaas ugaate hain.
served.answer: Mehrgarh (c. 7000 BCE) → Harappan cotton (c. 2600 BCE) → Kallanai (c. 2nd century CE) → Green Revolution (1960s).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can locate India’s neighbouring countries and describe shared geography, history and culture
served.prompt: Name the countries that share a land border with India.
served.prompt_hi: Un deshon ke naam batao jinki seema Bharat se zameen par milti hai.
served.answer: Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can locate India’s neighbouring countries and describe shared geography, history and culture
served.prompt: Through which countries does the Brahmaputra flow?
served.prompt_hi: Brahmaputra kin deshon se hokar behti hai?
served.answer: China (Tibet), India and Bangladesh

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can locate India’s neighbouring countries and describe shared geography, history and culture
served.prompt: Using a map, say in which direction each lies from India: Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Myanmar, Bhutan, the Maldives.
served.prompt_hi: Map dekh ke batao ki har desh Bharat se kis disha mein hai: Nepal, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Myanmar, Bhutan, Maldives.
served.answer: Nepal – north; Bangladesh – east; Sri Lanka – south (south-east of the tip); Pakistan – west/north-west; Myanmar – east; Bhutan – north-east; Maldives – south-west.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe major kingdoms of this period (such as the Pallavas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Palas) and their contributions
served.prompt: Which king ruled from Kanauj in the early 7th century, and which Chinese pilgrim visited his kingdom?
served.prompt_hi: 7vi shatabdi ki shuruaat mein Kanauj se kis raja ne raaj kiya, aur kaunsa Chini teerthyatri uske rajya mein aaya?
served.answer: Harsha (Harshavardhana), who ruled 606–647 CE; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe major kingdoms of this period (such as the Pallavas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Palas) and their contributions
served.prompt: In the first half of the 7th century, which of these were powerful at the same time?
served.prompt_hi: 7vi shatabdi ke pehle aadhe hisse mein inme se kaun ek saath shaktishaali the?
served.answer: Harsha in the north, the Chalukyas in the Deccan and the Pallavas in the south

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe major kingdoms of this period (such as the Pallavas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas and Palas) and their contributions
served.prompt: Name the century for each: Harsha's reign (606–647 CE); the Kailasa temple at Ellora (built in the 700s CE); Rajaraja Chola's temple at Thanjavur (completed around 1010 CE).
served.prompt_hi: Har ek ki shatabdi batao: Harsha ka shaasan (606–647 CE); Ellora ka Kailasa mandir (700s CE mein bana); Thanjavur mein Rajaraja Chola ka mandir (lagbhag 1010 CE mein poora hua).
served.answer: Harsha – 7th century CE; Kailasa temple – 8th century CE; Thanjavur temple – 11th century CE.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe political changes of the 11th and 12th centuries, including the Cholas and invasions from the north-west
served.prompt: Who built the Brihadeeswara temple, where, and about when was it completed?
served.prompt_hi: Brihadeeswara mandir kisne banwaaya, kahan, aur lagbhag kab poora hua?
served.answer: The Chola king Rajaraja I, at Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu, completed around 1010 CE.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe political changes of the 11th and 12th centuries, including the Cholas and invasions from the north-west
served.prompt: What did Mahmud of Ghazni mainly do in India?
served.prompt_hi: Ghazni ke Mahmud ne Bharat mein mukhya roop se kya kiya?
served.answer: He raided many times and carried wealth back to Ghazni, ruling only parts of the north-west such as Punjab

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can describe political changes of the 11th and 12th centuries, including the Cholas and invasions from the north-west
served.prompt: On a map of Chola power, describe in words how far their campaigns and influence reached from their home in Tamil Nadu.
served.prompt_hi: Chola shakti ke map ko dekh ke shabdon mein batao ki Tamil Nadu ke apne ghar se unke abhiyaan aur prabhaav kahan tak pahunche.
served.answer: From the Kaveri delta in Tamil Nadu they controlled much of south India, conquered northern Sri Lanka, reached the Maldives, marched north as far as the Ganga in Bengal, and sent a naval expedition across the Bay of Bengal to Southeast Asia (the Malay peninsula and Sumatra).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain how many communities and faiths came to live in India and enriched its culture
served.prompt: Name three communities that came from other lands and settled on India's west coast.
served.prompt_hi: Teen samudaayon ke naam batao jo doosre deshon se aakar Bharat ke pashchimi tat par base.
served.answer: Any three of: Jews (Kochi and the Konkan), Syrian Christians (Kerala), Parsis (Gujarat), Arab traders and early Muslim communities (Malabar coast), Siddis (Gujarat and Karnataka).

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain how many communities and faiths came to live in India and enriched its culture
served.prompt: Kochi's Paradesi Synagogue was built in 1568, and Kerala's Christian and Jewish communities are far older still. What does this show?
served.prompt_hi: Kochi ka Paradesi Synagogue 1568 mein bana tha, aur Kerala ke Isaai aur Yahoodi samudaay isse bhi bahut puraane hain. Isse kya pata chalta hai?
served.answer: India has been home to many faiths and communities for many centuries

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain how many communities and faiths came to live in India and enriched its culture
served.prompt: Describe, in time order and with places, these arrivals as a timeline in words: Parsis at Sanjan (about 8th–10th century CE); Christians in Kerala (tradition from the 1st century CE); Tibetans in Dharamshala (1959); a copper-plate grant to Kochi's Jewish leader (about 1000 CE).
served.prompt_hi: In aagmanon ko samay ke kram mein, jagahon ke saath, shabdon wali timeline ki tarah batao: Sanjan mein Parsi (lagbhag 8vi–10vi sadi CE); Kerala mein Isaai (parampara ke anusaar 1st sadi CE); Dharamshala mein Tibbati (1959); Kochi ke Yahoodi neta ko taamrapatra (lagbhag 1000 CE).
served.answer: Christians in Kerala (tradition from the 1st century CE) → Parsis at Sanjan, Gujarat (about 8th–10th century) → copper-plate grant to the Jewish leader in Kerala (about 1000 CE) → Tibetans in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh (1959).

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The State, the Government, and You
served.topic: The State, the Government, and You
outcomes: Learner can distinguish the state and the government and describe how government affects daily life
served.prompt: What are the four features of a state?
served.prompt_hi: Ek rajya (state/desh) ki chaar visheshtaayein kya hain?
served.answer: Population, territory, government and sovereignty.

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The State, the Government, and You
served.topic: The State, the Government, and You
outcomes: Learner can distinguish the state and the government and describe how government affects daily life
served.prompt: After a general election, a different party forms the government. What changes?
served.prompt_hi: Aam chunaav ke baad ek alag party sarkaar banati hai. Kya badalta hai?
served.answer: The government changes; the state — India, with its people, territory and sovereignty — stays the same

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: The State, the Government, and You
served.topic: The State, the Government, and You
outcomes: Learner can distinguish the state and the government and describe how government affects daily life
served.prompt: What is the difference between the state and the government?
served.prompt_hi: Rajya (state) aur sarkaar (government) mein kya fark hai?
served.answer: The state is the lasting political community — India with its people, territory and sovereignty. The government is the set of people and institutions that run the state at a given time; it changes through elections, while the state continues.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain why roads, railways, power and digital networks matter for development
served.prompt: What is infrastructure? Give four examples.
served.prompt_hi: Infrastructure kya hai? Chaar example do.
served.answer: The basic facilities a country needs to function, such as roads, railways, electricity, water supply, ports, airports, mobile and internet networks, schools and hospitals.

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain why roads, railways, power and digital networks matter for development
served.prompt: Which of these are infrastructure?
served.prompt_hi: Inme se kaun-kaun infrastructure hai?
served.answer: Roads, power lines, mobile towers, schools and hospitals — all of them

served.subject: sst
outcomes: Learner can explain why roads, railways, power and digital networks matter for development
served.prompt: Sort into physical or social infrastructure: road, hospital, power line, school, mobile tower, port, primary health centre, water pipeline.
served.prompt_hi: Inhe physical ya social infrastructure mein baanto: sadak, aspataal, bijli ki line, school, mobile tower, bandargaah (port), praathmik swaasthya kendra, paani ki pipeline.
served.answer: Physical: road, power line, mobile tower, port, water pipeline. Social: hospital, school, primary health centre.

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: Banks and the Magic of Finance
served.topic: Banks and the Magic of Finance
outcomes: Learner can describe what banks do, savings and loans, and simple interest in everyday terms
served.prompt: What are the two main jobs of a bank?
served.prompt_hi: Bank ke do mukhya kaam kya hain?
served.answer: Accepting deposits (keeping people's money safe) and giving loans (also helping with payments).

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: Banks and the Magic of Finance
served.topic: Banks and the Magic of Finance
outcomes: Learner can describe what banks do, savings and loans, and simple interest in everyday terms
served.prompt: What does a bank usually do with the money people deposit?
served.prompt_hi: Log jo paisa jama karte hain, bank aam taur par uske saath kya karta hai?
served.answer: Keeps part of it safe as a reserve and lends the rest to borrowers, earning interest

served.subject: sst
served.chapter: Banks and the Magic of Finance
served.topic: Banks and the Magic of Finance
outcomes: Learner can describe what banks do, savings and loans, and simple interest in everyday terms
served.prompt: What is the Reserve Bank of India, and what is one of its jobs?
served.prompt_hi: Reserve Bank of India kya hai, aur uska ek kaam kya hai?
served.answer: India's central bank, set up in 1935; it issues currency notes, regulates and supervises banks (it is the "banker's bank") and manages the country's money supply.
